## Data Sharing Setup
id="mc-main-content">
Data Sharing Setup
The Data Sharing feature allows up to 16 Panthers to share data.
Prerequisites
- Must be on System SW v7 or higher
- Firewall 5506-X must be configured for Data Sharing
Procedure
Note—
If a Panther System in a Data Sharing Group needs to have its software upgraded, the System MUST be removed from its Data Sharing Group before upgrading.
Note—
For customers on HSCN (UK NHS Network Only) running Remote Diagnostics while in a Data Sharing Group: ALL Systems in the Data Sharing Group MUST have the HSCN (N3) Remote Desktop Protocol installed.
Note—
If a PC in a Data Sharing Group needs to be re-imaged, the PC  MUST  be removed from its Data Sharing Group before re-imaging.
Reimaging MUST follow these steps in order:
- If tests are to be retained after re-imaging backup the Database .
Tests that were not backed will be lost.
- Remove the instrument from its data sharing group
- Re-Image
- Install All applicable SW
- If database was backed-up, restore the database from Step 1.
- Run Instrument Setup
- Add instrument to Data Sharing Group
Note—
When adding a Panther to a Data Sharing group, that Panther MUST  be in the Setup state.
The process of joining a group cannot complete unless the Panther to be joined is in the Setup state.
If the Panther to be added is not in the Setup State, that Panther will go to Data Access Only mode.
If this occurs, restart the Panther and ensure it is in the Setup state.
Note— Enabling Data Sharing will pull in user account information, valid reagent kits, and any master lots that may be needed for the kits.
Note— Once a group is joined, all historical data (including results) residing in the database cannot be accessed.
In order for the customer to access any data generated prior to joining a group, they must first disable data sharing.
Note—
All data generated while in a data sharing group can only be accessed while the Panther is a member of that group.
If the Panther leaves the group, that data can no longer be accessed, including results.
The Panther must rejoin the group in order to access any generated data.
Enabling Data Sharing in the Panther GUI
- Power on the Instrument and PC.
- Log in to the Panther GUI
- Enable Data Sharing
- Navigate to Tasks > Perform Maintenance > Service > Panther Link Features > Enable Data Sharing
- Shutdown and Restart the Panther GUI.
Create a Data Sharing Group
- Power on all Panther Systems and PCs.
- Log in to the Panther GUI
- Navigate to Admin >> Data Sharing Configuration .
- Click on Data Sharing Configuration icon.
- The screen below will appear.
- Select Create New Data Sharing Group .
- Create a New Group Name .
- Restart the Panther to create the Data Sharing Group.
Join a Data Sharing Group
- Log in to the next Panther's GUI.
-
Navigate to Admin >> Data Sharing Configuration .
- Click on Data Sharing Configuration icon.
- The screen below will appear.
- Select Join a Data Sharing Group .
- Select desired Data Sharing Group from the list.
- Click Join .
- The system will require a restart.
- Repeat 1-4 for all remaining Panther Systems.

## Firewall Wizard
id="mc-main-content">
Firewall Wizard
Parts and Materials Required
- Proper PPE
- Completed Site Assessment Form
- FSE Laptop
- Firewall Wizard Software
- Ethernet Cable 3m/10ft [To be purchased by FSEs]
- USB A to Mini USB (5506-X only)
- USB to Serial Cable [To be purchased by FSEs]
- RS232 to RJ45 Console Cable
- Cisco ASA Firewall 5506-X
OR
- Cisco ASA 5505
- Cisco SG112-24 Switch (If more than 1 instrument)
Time Required
- 1 Hour
Procedure
Part A: Installing Firewall Wizard Software
Part B: Connecting the Cisco ASA 5505/5506 to FSE Laptop
Part C: Programming the Firewall
Part D: Setting a Panther IP Address on the Panther Workstation
Part E: Hardware Setup after Firewall has been configured
- Cisco 5505 ASA
- Cisco 5506 ASA

## Installing the Firewall Wizard
id="mc-main-content">
Installing the Firewall Wizard
This section describes how to install the Firewall Wizard Software.
Note— Screen shots below are for reference ONLY .
Your screens may differ.
Uninstall any previous versions of the Firewall Wizard Software on the FSE laptop prior to installing the new Firewall Wizard Software.
- Close all running applications on the FSE Laptop.
- Download and save the appropriate Firewall Wizard version from Agile or BOX
Check with the relevant System Software TB for BOX address and SHA values.
- Unzip the .zip file.
- Double click on setup.exe to launch the Firewall Wizard installer.
- Click Run on the warning pop-up window, if it appears.
- Click Next> on the Welcome to the Firewall Wizard Screen.
- Select a folder to install the software locally on the laptop.
- Click Next> to continue.
- A pop-up may occur to install Microsoft .NET Framework 4.6.2 (x86 and x64) .
- Click Accept .
- This process may take up to 5 minutes and will require a restart.
- The Installation Complete page will appear if the software is installed correctly.
- Click Close to exit the Firewall Wizard installation.
- Verify that there is an icon on your desktop labeled Shortcut to FirewallWizard.exe .
Proceed to Connecting the Cisco ASA 5505/5506 to FSE Laptop

## Connecting the Cisco ASA 5505/5506 to FSE Laptop
id="mc-main-content">
Connecting the Cisco ASA 5505/5506 to FSE Laptop
- Connect the included Power Supply to the Cisco ASA 5505/5506 and a wall outlet.
- Connect the Console Cable to the Console Port on the ASA 5505/5506.
Note—The Blue Console port MUST be used.
No other port will establish a connection.
- Connect the FSE laptop to the Console port of the Firewall
- For the 5505, connect the Console Cable to the USB to Serial Adapter Cable.
- For the 5506-X, you many use a USB to Serial Adapter cable (as in Step 3a)
OR
use the provided USB to Mini USB cable to directly connect to the console port.
- Plug the USB end of the cable into the FSE laptop.
- Confirm the Cisco ASA 5505/5506 is ON by checking that the POWER, STATUS, and ACTIVE lights are on .
Proceed to Programming the Firewall

## Programming the Firewall
id="mc-main-content">
Programming the Firewall
This procedure applies to the Cisco ASA 5505 and Cisco ASA 5506 Firewalls.
Caution—If you are setting up a System with LINK, a 5506 is required.
Note:
Screen shots below are for reference ONLY . Your screens may differ.
All information entered into the Firewall Wizard will come from the Panther Site Assessment.
Only steps that require further action are described.
If selecting no and no further input is needed, it is not described.
Warning— PART B - Connecting the Cisco ASA 5505/5506 to FSE Laptop
MUST BE COMPLETED BEFORE CONTINUING
- Open the Firewall Wizard.
- Confirm Steps 1-4 have been completed and select Next > .
- Select the action you would like to perform.
- Configure Firewall.
- Configure Firewall but start with a saved configuration file.
Note: You can only use a saved configuration that was saved with firewall wizard 6.0.1.4
- Save the current Firewall configuration.
- Select an Output Directory location. Select Next .
- At the Serial Port Connected to Firewall screen, let the test run. After the test finishes, select Next .
- When finished, select Exit .
- Select Exit .
- Navigate to the output directory location you specified earlier.
Note: This is where you can find the output.txt file saved from performing this action.
Note: This will save an output.txt file. Information found in this file must be extracted for reuse.
- Install new Firewall OS (5506 only).
Note: The Install new Firewall OS will be used to install updates that are needed to fix vulnerabilities in the Cisco Operating System.
This will allow the firewall to install Cisco Operating System updates and provide protection against newly discovered vulnerabilities.
- Select Output Directory Location.
- Select Next , if the default location is acceptable
- To choose a different location, select Change .
- Select Make New Folder .
- Enter the folder name and select OK .
- Select Next. .
- Verify Firewall SW connection to your laptop.
Note: Automatic Connection Verification
When advancing from the Output Directory Location page to the Serial Port Connected to Firewall Page an automatic connection search will begin.
- A text box will indicate Connecting to Firewall .
- If successful, the following screen below will appear:
Note: IOS = Version,
ASDM = Version and MAC address of the firewall will be displayed.
- If not successful, follow the Testing the Serial Port Connection steps below:
Testing the Serial Port Connection
- Check that all connections are correct: Power, USB, and Serial.
- If connected correctly, select the Port drop-down menu.
- The Port drop-down menu will display all open ports and found.
- Select the COM Port that the Firewall is connected to.
- Click Test .
- The text box will indicate Testing Connection to COMX where X is the COM port number selected.
- The test will automatically connect to the Firewall and if successfully connected, the textbox will display:
Connection OK. IOS = Version. ASDM = Version. MAC = address
- Click Next when the connection is established.
- Enter the Site Information.
Note: By filling in the Site Information page, the wizard will program and record where the firewall is installed and who installed it.
This information is programed directly onto the firewall and listed in an instructions.txt file as an output of programing the firewall.
Complete the following fields.
- Site Name
- Your Full Name
- Firewall Serial # (located on the bottom of the firewall)
- Select the PANTHER radio button in the Hologic Instrument Model box
- Enter the number of instruments requiring connection to the Firewall.
Note: A maximum of 16 systems can connect to the Firewall.
- Select Next .
- Complete Cisco Syslog Setup.
Note:
Cisco network devices use Syslog to send system messages and debug output to a local logging process inside the device.
Cisco Syslog is a standard for logging messages.
Syslog allows the customer's IT/IS to monitor what the firewall is doing.
- Select Yes if the customer requests Syslog to be enabled.
- Enter the appropriate IP Address and Port.
- Select Next .
- Enable Windows Update Server.
Note: The Windows Update Server will be used to send Windows Updates that are needed to fix vulnerabilities in the Windows Operating System.
This will allow connected Panther Systems to install Operating System updates and provide protection against newly discovered vulnerabilities.
- Select Yes if the customer requests Windows Update Server to be enabled then select Next .
- Create a Read-only User Account.
Note:
The Read-Only User Account allows a customer to read the Firewall's configuration but does not allow them to modify settings.
The Read-Only User Account allows the customer's IT to access the Firewall with Read Only privileges and view the configuration.
The User Name will always default to "readonly" and may not be changed. Passwords must contain 4 to 32 characters.
- Select Yes if the customer requests a Read-only User Account then select Next .
- Enter the password provided by the customer in both the Password and Confirm Password fields then select Next .
- VPN Setup (Only applicable on the 5506)
Note:
VPN connections are only necessary at customer sites when Panthers are physically separated and cannot be physically connected to a single switch.
If the customer’s Ethernet infrastructure allows separated Panthers to be connected to a single switch, VPN is not needed.
The maximum number of VPN connections is 10.
Each physical location will require a Firewall installed.
If setting up a VPN, the external IP addresses of each Firewall MUST have a static IP address provided by the customer.
- Select Yes if the customer has Panthers at different physical locations that are to be connected.
- Specify the total number of locations (Firewalls) and select Next .
- Enter the External IP Address, External IP Mask, and External Gateway IP for each location and select Next.
Caution— Make sure to select Current Firewall for the Firewall you are programming.
- Obtain an External Interface IP Address.
Note: The Firewall must obtain an IP address from the customer network.
Three ways of obtaining an IP address are:
1. Dynamic Address - DHCP :
DHCP Gateway - A DHCP Server will administer an IP address to the firewall.
DHCP Range - A DHCP Server will administer an IP address to the firewall within a specified range of addresses.
2. Static IP - A Static IP address will be administered by the customer for the firewall to use as its IP address.
- Dynamic Address - DHCP
- For DHCP Gateway or DHCP Range, select the DHCP  radio button then select Next .
- Dynamic IP Address - DHCP Gateway
A DHCP Server will administer an IP address to the firewall.
Note: In some cases, a customer site may require a reservation within their DHCP server. If a customer requires a MAC address or physical address, the MAC address of the firewall is in the Serial Port Connected to Firewall page.
- Select Use Gateway if the customer requests DHCP Gateway and select Next .
- Enter the Gateway IP Address and select Next .
- Dynamic IP Address — DHCP Range
A DHCP Server will administer an IP address to the firewall within a specified range of addresses.
- Select Use IP Address Range if the customer requests DHCP Range and select Next.
- Enter the starting and ending IP addresses and select Next .
- Static IP Address (Permanent IP address)
A Static IP address will be administered by the customer for the firewall to use as its IP address.
- Select Static IP Address if the customer requests Static IP and select Next .
- Enter the Firewall IP Address , Firewall IP Subnet Mask , and Default Gateway then select Next .
- Domain Name Server (DNS) Settings
Note:
A Domain Name Server is used to resolve a hostname such as connect.hologicsecurecare.com to an IP address.
Open DNS (208.67.222.220) and Google DNS (8.8.8.8) are pre-populated by default.
- Verify the following check mark box is selected for:
Note: This should only be unchecked if connecting to the Hologic Network (internal).
- Populate a new Preferred DNS in the text box if provided.
- Populate a new Alternate DNS in the text box if provided.
- Select Next .
- Network Printer
Note:
There are two possibilities for networking the printer.
Option 1 is to network through the customer network.
An IP Address for the printer will be required from the customer.
Option 2 is to network within the Hologic network.
If Option 2 is needed, select NO when asked if the network printer will be used outside the firewall.
If the customer does not want the network printer on the customer’s network, there is the option for the printer to be connected to the switch.
Configure the IP address of the network printer to be 172.23.1.99,
subnet 255.255.255.0 and Gateway of 172.23.1.1
- Select Yes if the customer requests a Network Printer.
- Enter the IP Address of the Network Printer then select Next .
- Panther Link Dashboard Setup
Note:
Panther Link allows multiple Panthers to share a common database.
If setting up a Dashboard Server, a Cisco ASA 5506 MUST be used.
The Dashboard Server requires a static IP address on the customer’s network which will use NAT to connect to an internal Panther network IP address.
During this setup, the external (customer network) NAT IP address will need to be mapped.
The instructions.txt file will hold the necessary IP address and ports that will be used during configuration of the Dashboard server.
- Select Yes if the customer requests to be connected with Link Dashboard then select Next .
- Select Yes if the Dashboard Server will be connected to the Firewall currently being configured.
- Enter the Dashboard Server IP .
- Select Yes if the Dashboard Server will need to access Panthers connected to other Firewalls then select Next .
Note: Only necessary for VPN setups.
- Track System
Note:
With the addition of Track Systems, new network connections are required.
The Panther has integrated with two different track systems, IDS and Inpeco.
Note:
The Panther Trax solution requires network connections with WMS using an IDS track.
IDS does not require any additional input.
Note:
The Panther Track Ready System has the compatibility to be integrated and connected to a pre-existing Inpeco Track System. To connect to the Inpeco System, the customer technical support admin or the Inpeco Track System service organization will supply an External NAT IP Address as well as a dedicated port for each Panther that is to be connected to the track system.
- Select IDS - WMS if an IDS track will be connected to the firewall and select Next .
- Select Inpeco , if an Inpeco track will be connected to the firewall then select Next .
- Enter the External NAT IP Address for the Inpeco system.
- Enter the Interface Module Port for each Panther, then select the right arrow to add to the defined Interface Port List until all ports are mapped and click Next.
- Grifols Middleware
Note: Not for Hologic Track systems.
- Select Yes if the customer is using Grifols Middleware then select Next .
- Enter the Grifols IP Address and add the appropriate number of ports (1 per system), then select Next .
- Remote Diagnostics
Note:
TeamViewer and Grifols Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) are only used by Grifols.
RDXM and SecureLink do not require any additional input.
SecureLink will only work with System SW v7.2 and above.
You cannot connect multiple systems on a single firewall if they use SecureLink (System SW v7.2 and above) and RDXM/Pro360 (System SW v7.1 and below).
All systems with System SW v7.2 and above (SecureLink) can be connected on 1 Firewall.
All systems with System SW v7.1.5.4 and below (RDXM/Pro360) can be connected on 1 Firewall.
- Select the Remote Diagnostics method to be used at the customer site then select Next .
- HSCN (N3) Remote Desktop Protocol
Note: This is for UK NHS Network ONLY.
- Select the HSCN (N3) Remote Desktop Protocol radio button.
- Enter the HSCN IP Address then select Next .
- Enter the External NAT IP Address then select Next .
- Laboratory Information System (LIS)
Note: If LIS uses a serial connection, select No .
- Select Yes if LIS will be used then select Next .
- Select the LIS connections needed then select Next .
- LIS is Networked – For TCP/IP connections
- LIS uses Remote File Share
- For Pooling:
Note: Pooling will be configured with the use of a mapped network drive.
- TCP/IP LIS Connection: Check BOTH boxes
- Serial LIS Connection: Check LIS uses Remote File Share
- LIS Uses Remote File Share
- Enter the IP address , or addresses, for the mapped network drive then select Next .
- Enter the LIS IP Address and the port for each system then select Next .
Note: WMS to LIS Port will only appear if IDS - WMS was selected for Track System .
- To configure a Test LIS Server, enter the Networked LIS IP Address and LIS Port Mapping information. Select the check box then Next .
-
Enter the Test LIS IP Address and Test LIS Port for each system and select Next .
Note: WMS to LIS Test Port will only appear if IDS - WMS was selected for Track System .
- Review Your Input
- Review your input then select Configure.
Note: DO NOT click the Abort button unless it is necessary to cancel the configuration.
- Once the configuration is complete, verify the settings are correct and select OK .
- Upload the four configuration files shown below to the SR in Oracle or Panther Asset page in H1.
- Proceed to Setting a Panther IP Address on the Panther Workstation

## Setting a Panther IP Address on the Panther Workstation
id="mc-main-content">
Setting a Panther IP Address on the Panther Workstation
Complete the following on each Panther.
NOTE —
IP Addresses and Screenshots listed below are for reference ONLY .
- Log into the FSE Shield.
- Click the Command Prompt button.
- Enter " control ncpa.cpl " into the Command Prompt window and press Enter .
- Select the Local Area Connection that is currently enabled
- Position the mouse pointer over the enabled Local Area Connection ,
click the right mouse button, and select Select Properties .
- Select the Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) .
- Click Properties .
- Select Use the following IP Address:
NOTE —
IP Addresses and Screenshots listed below are for reference ONLY .
Use the instructions.txt file generated after Firewall has been programmed.
- Enter one of the generated IP addresses from the Firewall Wizard in the instructions.txt file.
- Enter 255.255.255.0 in the Subnet field.
- Enter X.X.X.1 in the Gateway field , where the X's are the same first 3 octets of the IP address.
Generally, this will be 172.23.1.1.
- If a DNS is specified follow the instructions below, otherwise select Obtain DNS server address automatically .
- If the DNS's were provided - Enter the Preferred DNS and Alternate DNS to match the instructions.txt file and the Site Assessment.
Proceed to Hardware Setup after the Firewall has Been Configured
- Click here if using a Cisco 5505 Firewall
- Click here if using a Cisco 5506 Firewall

## Cisco 5505 Hardware Setup after Firewall has Been Configured
id="mc-main-content">
Cisco 5505 Hardware Setup after Firewall has Been Configured
- Set the Cisco ASA 5505 firewall in a central location near the customers network port and electrical power.
- Connect the Firewall and switch to a power outlet.
- On the FSE laptop in which the firewall was configured on, open the instructions.txt file.
- Connect an Ethernet cable from the customers network port to Port 0 of the Cisco ASA 5505 Firewall.
- If only ONE Panther is being networked, connect Port 7 of the Cisco ASA 5505 Firewall to the Ethernet Port of the Panther PC
- If multiple Panthers are being networked:
- first connect Port 24 of the SG112-24 Cisco Switch to Port 7 of the Cisco ASA 5505 Firewall.
- then connect all Panthers to the Switch starting at Port 1 to Port 10.
Note— The order/port does not matter.
Note—
The Cisco 5505 can ONLY support up to 10 instrument connections
- Setting a Panther IP Address on the Panther Workstation provided from the instructions.txt file.
Caution—It is important to remember which IP address is assigned to each instrument.
- On each Panther, configure the LIS Port Number with its respective number.
Note— LIS Port numbers are mapped to specific Instruments/Panther IP addresses.

## Cisco 5506 Hardware Setup after Firewall has Been Configured
id="mc-main-content">
Cisco 5506 Hardware Setup after Firewall has Been Configured
- Set the Cisco ASA 5506 firewall in a central location near the customers network port and electrical power.
- Connect the Firewall to a power outlet.
- Connect an Ethernet cable from the customers network port to Port 1 of the Cisco ASA 5506 Firewall.
- If installing a Dashboard Server, connect an Ethernet cable from the Server to Port 2 of the Firewall
- If only ONE Panther is being networked, connect Port 8 of the Cisco ASA 5506 Firewall to the Ethernet Port of the Panther PC
- If multiple Panthers are being networked:
- first connect Port 24 of the SG112-24 Cisco Switch to Port 8 of the Cisco ASA 5506 Firewall.
- then connect all Panthers to the switch starting at Port 1 to Port 16.
Note— The order/port does not matter.
- On the FSE laptop in which the firewall was configured on, open the instructions.txt file.
- Setting a Panther IP Address on the Panther Workstation provided from the instructions.txt file.
Caution—It is important to remember which IP address is assigned to each instrument.
- On each Panther, configure the LIS Port Number with its respective number.
Note— LIS Port numbers are mapped to specific Instruments/Panther IP addresses.

## Pipettor Pressure Integrity Test
id="mc-main-content">
Pipettor Pressure Integrity Test
Time Required
- 15 Minutes
Procedure
Any test result equal to 0.33 or above is a successful test result for the Pressure Integrity Test.
Screenshots are for reference only. Your screen may vary.
- Start up Service Software.
- Navigate to the System tab.
- In the Pressure Integrity Test section, select the Report checkbox. This instructs the system to generate a report of the results.
- In the Pressure Integrity Test section, check Initialize . This initializes all modules.
- Check the box next to Left Arm .
- Click Pressure Integrity Test .
The Report Setup screen appears .
- Enter your name for the login name and click OK .
A Service Software dialog box appears .
- Insert a DiTi cone cap into Position 1, Tip Tray 1, Tip Drawer 1
- Click OK .
- Different versions of Service Software will display different ranges for the Pressure Integrity Test Ratios.
Remember:
Any test result greater than 0.33 is a successful test result for the Pressure Integrity Test. See Sample Test Results below for reference.
- Repeat Steps 3–10 for the right pipettor arm.
- If this is an installation, continue to System Level Operational Qualification (OQ) .
Example Test Results
Note—
In some versions of Service Software, Test results over 1.00 will display as a "fail"; however, results over 1.00 are acceptable as a passing value.

## System Bootup
id="mc-main-content">
System Bootup
See the Panther System Operator's Manual for detailed information.
- Open the Panther System main software and verify that the system boots without errors.
- Load MTUs into the MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station. Input Queue.
- Load tips into the Tip Drawers.
- Load the following fluids: Auto Detect 1, Auto Detect 2, Bleach, Buffer, and Oil.
- Install the Universal Fluid bottle connectors.
- Install the waste bottle, waste bag, and waste deflector.
- Continue to Panther GUI Software Configuration .

## Panther System Operational Qualification (OQ)
id="mc-main-content">
Panther System Operational Qualification (OQ)
Parts and Materials Required
- 2 MTUs per each OQ cycle
Time Required
- Clear MTUs—10 minutes
- OQ cycle—25 minutes
Procedure
- Put on proper PPE.
- Open Service Software .
- Navigate to the System tab.
- If needed, select the Clear MTUs checkbox. This instructs the system to check for any MTUs that may be present in any of the system's modules.
- Check Report to generate a report of the results.
- Check Initialize to initialize all modules.
- Check the All modules box.
- Select 2 under Cycles. This indicates two full OQ cycles. Additional cycles can be run if needed.
- Click System OQ Test .
The system initializes, clears all MTUs, and starts the OQ test .
When the OQ test finishes, a report of the results appears on the screen .
- Enter any useful information in the Comments field.
- Click OK to save the file.
- Create a name for the file and save it onto the Panther System PC Workstation.
- If this is an installation, continue to System Bootup .

## Install the MTU Sidecar Covers
id="mc-main-content">
Install the MTU Sidecar Covers
- Load all MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station.  Carriers into the Sidecar.
Note— You can move a carrier to the MTU Queue or loading position via service software.
- Locate the blue door cover.
- Secure the door cover to the MTU Sidecar using the 6 Philips screws included with the Kit.
- Secure the Hand-held bar code scanner bracket to the blue top cover with the 2 included screws.
- Attach the USB cable and USB hub power cable to the USB hub board on the top cover.
- Route these cable through the cable harness / cable guides.
- Connect the Status LED on the top cover to the PCB located on the back of the MTU Sidecar.
- Install the MTU Sidecar Top panel and align the top cover so that it is centered on the keyway of the sidecar.
- Adjust the top cover so that the face of the loading door and top cover are flush.
If needed, adjust the hardstops to align the face of the loading door and top cover so they are flush.
- Secure the top cover with four screws and washers.
- Install the screw in the middle of the cover.
- Open the MTU Carrier Loading Door and loosen the two screws securing the hard stop guard.
- Remove the hard stop guard and install the provided screw and washer in the front of the cover.
- Re-install the hard-stop guard using the screws loosened in the previous step.
- Close the loading door.
- Locate the front cover.
- Insert the front cover at an angle to slide the front cover under the top cover.
- Push the bottom of the front cover to secure the cover in the snap clips.
Note— You may have to adjust the marketing panel.
- Open the loading door and pull out the drawer to access the screw hole used to secure the front cover.
- Secure the front cover with the provided screw.
- Locate the side cover.
- Slide the side panel pins into the slots on the side of the MTU Sidecar.
- Slide the panel to the left and then push on the bottom of the panel to secure the snap clips.
- Locate the MTU Sidecar back.
- Install the Back Cover of the MTU Sidecar.
- Loosely Install the bottom two Screws.
- Slide the Back plate over the two bottom screws
- Loosely install 3 additional screws.
Note— The middle screw location closest to the Panther is to be left empty.
- Loosely secure the Side Panel to the Back Plate using the included screw.
- Tighten all 6 screws to secure the backplate.
- Install the Side Panther Cover behind the MTU Sidecar.
You may need to move the Hinge Plate Upwards for clearance to install the door.
- Install the side Panther Upper Cover.
- Route the monitor cables out of the Upper Cover and tighten the cable clamps.
- Secure the door in place using the screw located on the inside of the Panther chassis.
- Install the MTU Queue Cover.
- Plug in the handheld barcode scanner.
- Proceed to MTU Expansion Installation Verification

## MTU Expansion Installation Verification
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Expansion Installation Verification
- Open Service Software.
- Ensure all MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station.  Carriers are loaded into the sidecar. For this OQ, all six carriers must be loaded.
You can move a carrier to the MTU Queue or loading position via service software.
- Click on the P-System tab.
- Click on the MTU Expansion tab.
- Change the number of Cycles to 3 .
- Ensure that Report AND Initialize are checked.
- Click on MTU Expansion OQ Test to start the test.
- A pop up will appear asking to load at least 1 MTU. Insert one MTU and click OK .
- The OQ Test will begin.
- After each OQ cycle is completed, you will be required to insert at least 1 MTU and click OK .
Caution—Failure to pick or place a carrier results in a failed Operational Qualification.
- If all 3 OQ cycles are completed without an error, save the report to a flash drive for attachment to the Installation Record.
- MTU Expansion Installation is complete.

## MTU Expansion Installation
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Expansion Installation
To install a PLUS module, the System requires the following:
- Panther Plus can only be installed on Panther Systems Serial #00375 and above.
- PCAP Monitor required if installing MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station.  Expansion ONLY
- Dell XE3
- Software v7.x and above
- Waste to Drain - drain must be able to handle a minimum flowrate of 1L/min.
- Waste to Drain - drain must be 15m (49ft) or less from the Waste to Drain pump.
- Waste to Drain - drain must be no higher than 1.2m (3.9ft) from the floor
Parts and Materials Required
- Proper PPE
- Panther Tool Kit
- Level
- System Software
- Panther Plus v7.1.5 or higher
- Panther Fusion Plus v7.2.1 or higher
- PCAP Monitor Installed
- MTU EXPANSION KIT
- Dimensions
- (82cm x 122cm x 115cm @ 91kg)
- (32in x 48in x 45in @ 200lbs)
- MTU Sidecar
- MTU Sidecar Alignment Plate
- MTU Sidecar Rear Cover Plate
- MTU Sidecar Covers
- MTU Expansion Trim Pieces
- MTU Queue
- 5x MTU Carriers
- Panther Side Door
- Input Queue Cover
- Y-Splitter CAN Cable
- Male to Male CAN Cable
- MTU QUEUE TEACH TOOL [TLS-06904]
- INPUT QUEUE TEACH TOOL [TLS-06359]
- Cart for moving the MTU Expansion Module (Lab Supplied).
Time Required
- 3 Hours
Procedure
The sequence of installation is as follows
- Unboxing MTU Expansion
- Prepare the Panther
- MTU Queue Installation
- Teach the Linear Distributor to MTU Queue
- MTU Sidecar Installation
- Verify alignment in Y-Direction of scissor
- MTU Queue to Sidecar Alignment
- MTU Expansion Autoteach
- Install the Covers
Operational Qualification
- MTU Expansion Installation Verification

## MTU Expansion Unboxing
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Expansion Unboxing
- Locate the MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station.  Expansion pallet.
- Cut the restraining straps and set the largest box aside.
- Open the Assay Procedures required to prepare and perform a specific test. In the context of this document, assay refers exclusively to a Hologic test, such as Aptima Combo or Ultrio. MTU Sidecar Cover box.
- Remove all contents and set aside for installation.
Caution—Use caution when lifting the blue top cover. Use two hands and lift straight up.
- Unbox the two smaller boxes containing the MTU Queue and miscellaneous hardware.
Note— Set aside the Stratec Test Protocol sheet and keep for records.
- Open the bottom box on the palette. This should contain the MTU Sidecar.
- Set aside the Stratec Test Protocol sheet and keep for records.
- Remove the two smaller boxes containing the MTU Carriers.
- Locate the bottom of the MTU Sidecar.
- Unbox the MTU Sidecar.
- Close the box and stand on the side of the box closest to the top of the MTU Sidecar.
- Slide the box off the end of the palette while lifting as shown in the image below.
- Continue lifting the box so that it is standing on the side closest to the bottom of the MTU Sidecar.
- Open the box to expose the MTU Sidecar.
- Remove the top layer of foam surrounding the MTU Sidecar.
- Tilt the top of the MTU Sidecar out of the box and lift from the locations shown below to remove it from the box.
- Place the MTU Sidecar on the floor and inspect that there is no damage from shipping.
- Move the MTU Sidecar and additional parts via a lab supplied cart to a workspace near the Panther to be upgraded.
- Proceed to Preparing the Panther

## Prepare the Panther for MTU Expansion
id="mc-main-content">
Prepare the Panther for MTU Expansion
Procedure
- Power down the Panther System.
- Remove the right-side door.
- Remove and discard the lower trim and mounting trim.
- Remove and discard the rear corner trim piece.
- Remove the back trim piece.
- Install the lower profile cover onto the back trim piece.
- Reinstall the back trim piece.
- Disconnect the cables to the PCAP monitor.
- Remove and save the cable clamps securing the monitor cables
- Route the cables away from the Monitor Arm and out of the cable channels.
- Remove the Hand-held Scanner Bracket.
- Remove the USB Hub Expansion Cover.
- Unplug the Power and USB cables AND discard the USB Hub Expansion Cover
- Route the Monitor and USB Hub cables into the Panther.
- Remove the USB Hub Expansion Cover Mounting Bracket.
- Remove the USB Hub cables from their routing through the Chassis frame.
- Release the USB Hub cables from the front cable clamp.
- Remove the black trim from the front right-side of the Panther.
- Remove and save this screw to be used again when installing the new bracket.
- Remove the door mounting brackets on the front right-side of the Panther.
- Remove the tube harness by collapsing the tabs and pushing down on the clip.
- Attach the L-bracket with the short-end pointing up, as shown below, using the included 2 screws and 2 washers.
- Install the new trim piece with screw removed in the previous step, into the top hole.
- Reroute the monitor cables, loosely install the lower and upper cable clamps, and connect to the monitor.
- Reorient the Chassis Fan
- Loosen the screws and remove the fan bracket.
Note— It may be easier to access the mounting screws by removing the fans from their bracket without unplugging the fans.
- Tighten the new Fan bracket into the Panther Chassis
- Install the fans on the new bracket oriented as shown below.
- Dress the wires as needed.
- Attach the Hinge Plate to the Panther Chassis.
- Unscrew the tube clamp securing the cooling tubing to the Panther Chassis.
- Move the tubing clamp and cooling tube away from the Panther Chassis to make room for the Hinge Plate.
- Place the Hinge Plate on the Panther Chassis and align with the screw hole used by the tube clamp.
- Locate the white cable clamp included with the MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station. Expansion kit.
- Loosely secure the tubing and cable clamp to the chassis using the longer screw included in the MTU Expansion Kit.
Note— Remove the Peristaltic Pump Assembly for better access to the screw, as needed.
- Install the Y-splitter CAN cable
- The new Y-Splitter CAN cable connects the MTU expansion module to the Panther by splitting a connection to the Pump Module
- Disconnect the right-most 6 pin CAN Cable on the Pump Module PCB.
- Connect the Male to Male Adapter to the Cable unplugged from the Pump Module PCB..
- Connect the Y-splitter CAN cable origin to the right-most 6 pin CAN plug on the Pump Module PCB.
- Move the connector above the Pump module and route the long-end of the CAN cable behind the clip that holds the injector tubing.
- Remove the Input Queue.
Note—If the Input Queue will be returned, decontaminate and complete Decon/OBF/RMA Form [19-02-APX-A]. Save the front and back mounting screws for installation of the MTU Queue in later steps.
Leave the front cover removed to install the MTU Queue.
- MTU Queue Installation

## MTU Queue Installation
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Queue Installation
- Remove the bag containing the countersunk screw taped to the top of the MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station.  Queue, and save for a later.
- Place the MTU Queue into the location previously occupied by the Input Queue.
- Loosely position the MTU Queue with 2 mounting screws on the front and back mounting locations with a 4 mm Hex key.
Note— Remove the flat washer from the rear position.
aa
- Loosely install MTU Queue center mounting location with the provided countersunk screw
- Connect the Input Queue CAN cable to the MTU Queue.
- Run Instrument Setup (Firmware)
Note— Connecting the MTU sidecar CAN cable at this point will save time.
- Power on the system and PC.
- Run Instrument Setup (Loading Firmware)
- Select all necessary instrument configurations when running Instrument Setup.
- Teach the Linear Distributor to MTU Queue.

## Teaching Linear Distributor to MTU Queue for Panther Plus
id="mc-main-content">
Teaching Linear Distributor to MTU Queue for Panther Plus
Auto Teach Linear Distributor to MTU Queue
- Move the Linear Distributor away from the MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station. Queue (i.e. chiller slot 1)
- Insert the black MTU Queue Teach Tool into the MTU Queue.
- Remove the Retention Clip on the Input Queue Teach Tool.
- Insert the MTU Input Queue Teach Tool into the pick position of the MTU Queue.
- Firmly push the Input Queue Teach Tool into the MTU Queue until it is firmly up against the MTU Sidecar Alignment Tool.
- Manually align MTU Queue such that the tab of the Teach Tool and the Hook are centered.
Note— See Using the Input Queue Autoteach Tool
- Select Position Teach MTU Input Queue or Auto Teach All .
- If Auto Teach All is selected for the Linear Distributor, ensure the service drawer is fully closed and latched.
- Allow the Linear Distributor to teach to the MTU Queue.
- Remove the Teach tools once teaching is complete.
- MTU Sidecar Installation
OR
Manual Teach Linear Distributor to MTU Queue
- Open Service Software.
- Loosen the 3 screws attaching the MTU Queue to the Panther Chassis
- One screw is located at the back of the MTU Queue.
- One screw is located at the front of the MTU Queue.
aa
- One screw is located on the bottom plate of the MTU Queue
- Initialize the Linear Distributor and Input Queue in Service Software.
Note— The MTU Queue is label Input Queue in Service Software.
- Perform the Theta Alignment procedure.
- Insert an MTU Carrier with a minimum of 2 MTUs into the MTU Queue.
- Click on the P-Front&Loading tab in Service Software.
- Click Push MTU .
- Click on the Linear Distributor tab.
- Click on Teach .
- Select Sledge in the Select Drive box.
- Select the Input Queue in the Select Position box.
- Select Move Theta & Z & X to selected Position (!! fast move!!) in the Options for selected Device and Drive.
- The Linear Distributor should be in position next to the MTU Queue.
- Select Move Hook to selected Position in the Options for selected Device and Drive.
- Click Execute .
- Physically position the MTU Queue so that the tab of the MTU and the Hook are centered.
- Tighten the 3 screws securing the MTU Queue loosened in the previous Step 2.
- MTU Sidecar Installation

## MTU Sidecar Installation
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Sidecar Installation
Procedure
- Close and lock the Service Drawer.
- Install the MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station.  Expansion Guide Plate.
- Remove the Guide Plate and any packing material from the MTU Sidecar. (e.g. belt clips, foam inserts.)
- Loosely re-attach the Guide Plate to the right-side of the Panther frame using a 2.5 mm Hex key and the 7 socket screws and washers provided.
These screws are taped to the Guide Plate.
Note—Ensure the wires and UFD Open/Close Sensor Cable are not crushed by the Guide Plate.
- Align the MTU Expansion Guide Plate to the MTU Queue
Note—Check that the Service Drawer latch unlocks with the MTU Expansion Guide Plate installed.
- Use the Guide Plate Alignment pin and the alignment features at the rear of the MTU Queue.
- If the alignment pin is centered between the two long tick marks, tighten the 7 low-profile screws.
Adjust as needed to center the alignment pin.
- Prepare the MTU Sidecar for mating to the Panther.
- Put the top cover on the sidecar, no need to tighten screws.
- Raise the feet to get the latches approximately centered in the cut outs and the Top Cover approximately even with the Panther TCR Target capture reagent—An assay-specific reagent added as part of specimen pipetting. door.
- Move the sidecar away from the system and loosely install the front Alignment Pin on the MTU Sidecar as shown below.
Warning—DO NOT LOOSEN THE TWO ALIGNMENT PINS AT THE
REAR OF THE MTU SIDECAR
- Slide the MTU Sidecar towards the system so that the front and top rear alignment pins mate with the alignment slots on the guide plate.
Note— Adjustment by hand, to the height of the feet, may be needed so that all three pins align to their slots.
- Adjust the outside feet to ensure the top of the MTU Sidecar is slightly tilted out from the right side of the Panther
- Adjust the feet as needed so that the lower pin slides into the rear into the slot with minimal force.
Warning— DO NOT LOOSEN THE REAR MTU SIDECAR PINS.
Note— Lowering both back feet will rotate the MTU sidecar clockwise when looking at it from the right side of the system. Raising both back feet will rotate the MTU sidecar counter clockwise when looking at it from the right side of the system.
Note— Lowering both front feet will rotate the MTU sidecar counter clockwise when looking at it from the right side of the system. Raising both front feet will rotate the MTU sidecar clockwise when looking at it from the right side of the system.
- Tighten the Front Pin.
Note— The front alignment pin can be moved into position from the inside of the MTU Sidecar.
- Remove the sidecar and re-install. The Sidecar should slide in with minimal force. If not adjust feet as needed.
- Push the top of the sidecar towards the system.
Close all latches and adjust the outside feet so that they are just touching the ground.
- Verify alignment in Y-Direction of scissor .

## Verify alignment in Y-Direction of scissor
id="mc-main-content">
Verify alignment in Y-Direction of scissor
- Make sure the Panther System is powered off.
- Insert the black MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station.  Queue Teach Tool into the MTU Queue.
- Raise the scissor lift to be level with the MTU Queue.
- Swing the carrier platform into the MTU Queue.
- Slightly lift the carrier platform so that the alignment pin is in the MTU Queue teach tool.
- Verify that the carrier platform is properly aligned using the MTU Queue teach tool.
- If the alignment front pin is not within the field goal, note the direction and how many tick marks it will take to center the pin to the field goal.
- Unfuse the MTU Sidecar.
- Loosen the Guide Plate screws.
- Use the direction and tick marks recorded in step 7 to realign the guide plate left or right, in order to center the MTU Queue alignment pin as shown in step 6.
- Tighten the Screws.
- Fuse the MTU Sidecar.
- Continue to MTU Queue to Sidecar Alignment

## MTU Queue to Sidecar Alignment
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Queue to Sidecar Alignment
- Make sure the Panther System is powered off.
- Insert the black MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station.  Queue Teach Tool into the MTU Queue.
- Raise the scissor lift to be level with the MTU Queue.
- Swing the carrier platform into the MTU Queue.
- Slightly lift the carrier platform so that the alignment pin is in the MTU Queue teach tool.
- Verify all four pins are in a line as shown in the image below.
- If the front pin on the scissor is to the left of the MTU Queue front pin, install shims as necessary behind the latch catches between the front of the Panther and sidecar.
- If the rear pin on the scissor is to the left of the MTU Queue rear pin, install shims as necessary behind the latch catches between the rear of the sidecar and Panther.
- Once shims are in place repeat as needed until the MTU Queue and carrier platform are aligned.
- Connect the CAN cable, USB cable and USB hub power cable to the board on the MTU Sidecar.
- Insert the MTU Expansion CAN cable, USB cable, and USB hub power cable into the white cable clamp.
- Route the cables as shown below and secure the clamps to the chassis using the longer screw included in the MTU Expansion Kit.
- Run Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- Power on the system and PC.
- Run Instrument Setup (Loading Firmware)
- Select all necessary instrument configurations when running Instrument Setup.
- Continue to MTU Expansion Autoteach

## MTU Expansion Autoteach
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Expansion Autoteach
- Power on the Panther system and PC.
- Start Service Software.
- Verify that MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station.  Expansion is a configured module on the Instrument Configuration page.
Note— If needed, reset the Panther Configuration by navigating the Main & Com. tab and click Reset Configuration .
- Remove all MTU carriers from the system.
- Set Authorization Code.
- Click on the IC-MTU Expansion tab.
- Click on the Parameter tab.
- Set Authorization Code to 1 .
- Select the Teach tab and verify MTU Lift is selected.
- Select Auto teach full (incl. MTU Queue) .
- Click Execute . The Auto Teach will now begin.
Note— A dialog box will appear asking if the carriers were removed from the MTU Expansion module. Verify to make sure there are no carriers in the module.
- After Auto Teach is complete, install ALL MTU Carriers in the MTU Expansion Module.
- Place MTU Carriers into any positions within the MTU Expansion module.
Note: There must be a carrier in the loading position to properly teach the end of the travel.
- Orient all MTU Carriers as shown below:
- Under Select Drive, select MTU Pusher .
- Select AutoTeach End of Travel .
- Click Execute . The Auto Teach will now begin.
Note— A dialog box will appear asking if the MTUs were removed from the carrier. Verify to make sure the carrier is empty.
- Continue to Install the MTU Sidecar Covers .

## Unboxing Waste on the Fly
id="mc-main-content">
Unboxing Waste on the Fly
-
- Dimensions of Waste on the Fly packaging
- (82cm x 122cm x 163cm @ 47kg)
- (32in x 48in x 64in @ 105lbs)
-
Note— Pictures below are for Reference ONLY. Your setup may differ.
- Locate the Panther Plus pallet.
