## Visual Dispense Verification Procedures
id="mc-main-content">
Visual Dispense Verification Procedures
Scope
A Visual Dispense Verification is a quick method to check the overall dispense of fluids within a module for approximate volume and consistency verification.
A Visual Dispense Verification can be performed in the Luminometer, the Magnetic Washes, and in some cases, in the Output Queue. This procedure is to be used as a troubleshooting tool only, and is not intended to be an accurate measurement.
Parts and Materials Required
- Service Software Beta 15 or later
Time Required
- 1 hour
Procedure
Startup Sequence
- Start up the system main assay software and let the system complete the unload sequence (Reference to the Operator's Manual).
- Verify that the initialization sequence is complete and goes into the unloading of MTUs.
- Prime Operation of pumping fluid through tubing to ensure proper and consistent fluid delivery (remove air from the tubing, etc.). the system (see the Panther System Operator's Manual ).
Output Queue Visual Dispense Verification
- Verify that MTUs are present and perform a system prime (Reference to the Operator's Manual).
- During the prime sequence, for the first MTUs, monitor the bleach and buffer lines to confirm that no leaks are present at the connections, pumps, and/or valves.
- Monitor the Output Queue as it dispenses fluid into the tube. Confirm each tube is receiving the same amount of fluid and that the module is placing the MTUs onto its stack properly and consistently.
Magnetic Wash Module Visual Dispense Verification
- Start up Service Software .
- Ensure that the vacuum system is Initialized and Activated .
- Ensure that the Mag Wash(es) are primed. If any fluid fittings have been loosened it will be necessary to prime. To prime a Mag Wash:
- Navigate to the Distributor tab and insert a new MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station. into the Magnetic Wash module.
- Pick tiplets from the MTU. Under the Move tab, select Pick Up to pick the tiplets .
- Navigate to the Sequence section under 7 Magnet Washer tab in Service Software, inject 2000 µL of wash buffer. Make sure to check all 5 tubes of the MTU. Be sure that you have selects the appropriate Mag Wash device (#1 or #2) .
- Confirm that the system is primed by checking for air bubbles in the lines. If the system is still not primed Aspirate the fluid from the MTU tube by pressing Aspirate. Then repeat steps a–d. Repeat these steps for oil if necessary and/or for the other Mag Wash.
- Use the linear distributor to remove the MTU from the Mag Wash. Eject the tiplets from the Mag Washes that have been primed by pressing Eject .
- Navigate to the Distributor tab and insert a new MTU into the Magnetic Wash module.
- In the Sequence section under 7 Magnet Washer tab in Service Software, inject 2000 µL of wash buffer, followed by 2000 µL of oil. Make sure to check all 5 tubes of the MTU. Be sure that you have selected the appropriate Mag Wash device (#1 or #2).
- Navigate the Distributor to place the MTU into the service queue for inspection.
- Inspect the MTU.
- The overall fluid level should be visually consistent across each tube.
- The dividing line between wash and oil should be noticeable and consistent across each tube.
- Air bubbles and foam in the liquid should be minimal.
- Using the service queue and the Distributor, place the filled MTU back into the Magnetic Wash module.
- Under the Move tab, select Pick Up to pick the tiplets.
- Confirm the vacuum is still active and select Aspirate .
- Once again, move the MTU to the service queue and inspect it to confirm the tiplets are missing and all the fluid has been aspirated from each tube.
- Dispose of the MTU and repeat the procedure with Magnetic Wash 2.
Luminometer Module Visual Dispense Verification
- Start up Service Software .
- Navigate to the 6. Luminometer tab.
- Confirm that the Luminometer contains no MTUs.
- Click Emergency Unload/Grab of the second MTU and follow the prompts.
- Use the Distributor to remove any MTUs left in the Luminometer.
- Place a new MTU in the module with the Distributor and use the Prime function under Sequence to prime the AD1 and AD2 lines to the injector.
- Check all AD1 and AD2 lines and connections and check for leaks at pumps and valves.
- Remove the MTU from the Luminometer to the service queue.
- Inspect the MTU for:
- The overall fluid level should be visually consistent across each tube.
- Air bubbles and foam in the liquid should be minimal.
- Start up the Panther System software and verify that once the system is in a steady state, the vacuum pressure reads between 6 and 7.

## Waste Bottle CPC Coupling Integrity Check
id="mc-main-content">
Waste Bottle CPC Coupling Integrity Check
What is Affected
Some white CPC couplings that secure the waste bottle to the waste mounting block have been over- torqued during manufacturing. This has resulted in cracks to the coupling that can cause low vacuum failures.
If the 2 couplings are the old polypropylene type (gray in color), Replace the Two Male Fittings in the Waste Drawer that Connect to the Waste Bottle and Tapping the Waste Bottle Mounting Block to upgrade the fittings to the new type.
Parts and Materials Required
- Proper PPE
- Panther Tool Kit
- If the CPC Coupling Integrity Check fails:
- 2x Waste Bottle CPC Coupling
Note—If one coupling is cracked, replace both.
Time Required
- 15 Minutes
Procedure
Part A: Inspect the CPC Coupling
- Put on proper PPE.
- Power down the Panther System.
- Open the Waste Drawer.
- Remove the waste bottle.
- Located the 2 CPC waste bottle couplings.
- If the two couplings are the old polypropylene type (gray in color), STOP  and Replace the Two Male Fittings in the Waste Drawer that Connect to the Waste Bottle and Tapping the Waste Bottle Mounting Block . Then verify installation by continuing to the next step.
- Inspect each CPC coupling.
- Check the integrity of the CPC couplings by using a gloved finger to apply a small amount of sideways force to each connector.
Note— If the connector is fractured below the surface it will flex and likely fall apart.
- Verify each coupling base is flush to the top of the waste manifold.
Note— If either CPC coupling is damaged or not flush, replace BOTH couplings.
Part B: Replace the CPC Couplings
- Remove the 2 existing CPC couplings.
Note— If either coupling is damaged or broken in the manifold, use a standard tapered extractor set (commercially available) to remove the coupling.
Caution—If the threads on the mounting block are damaged during removal, replace the Waste Bottle Mounting Block [MME-02598]
- Install a new set of CPC couplings [MME-02058]
Note—DO NOT over-tighten the new CPC couplings. Over-tightening will create cracks in the new coupling.
- Return the waste bottle to the drawer.
- Adjust the mounting block if necessary so the waste bottle is sitting flat in the drawer and the new couplings are fully engaged. Refer Tapping the Waste Bottle Mounting Block .
- Shut the waste drawer.
Verification
- Complete a system prime using the Panther Main software to verify that the vacuum system functions properly.

## Replace the Two Male Fittings in the Waste Drawer that Connect to the Waste Bottle
id="mc-main-content">
Replace the Two Male Fittings in the Waste Drawer that Connect to the Waste Bottle
What is Affected
The current polypropylene fittings have been found to degrade due to exposure to bleach. Over time the bleach can cause these fittings to crack under stress, resulting in spillage, possible contamination and low vacuum failures. The new fittings are made from Polysulfone. This material is known to have better material compatibility with bleach.
Parts and Materials Required
- Proper PPE
- Adjustable Wrench
- Waste Bottle CPC Coupling
Note— Make sure to order 2 if you need to replace the 2 fittings.
Time Required
- 20 Minutes
Procedure
- Put on proper PPE.
- Power down the Panther System.
- Open the Waste Drawer.
- Use an adjustable wrench to remove the 2 existing CPC waste bottle couplings in the drawer.
- Install the new Polysulfone CPC waste bottle couplings.
- Put the waste bottle back in the drawer.
- Close the waste drawer.
- Loosen the CPC fitting block mounted to the drawer and adjust it.
- Make sure the fittings are fully engaged and that the waste bottle is sitting flat in the drawer.
- Tighten the block to the drawer.
Verification
- Power on the Panther System.
- Open the Panther GUI.
- Monitor the vacuum pressure through the Panther GUI.
- After 5 minutes the Panther vacuum pressure should settle into a range of 7 in/Hg +/- 1 in/Hg.
- Verify that the system can successfully pass prime.

## Waste Bottle Rotational Floats Inspection Procedure
id="mc-main-content">
Waste Bottle Rotational Floats Inspection Procedure
What is Affected
Several Panther Waste Bottles, MN 903407 (Stratec PN 00100000025) were found to be defective when received in the field by FSE’s or customers. Currently, the known failure mode is broken rotational floats. Stratec was contacted and was informed of this defective and are currently working on a long term solution.
Parts and Materials Required
- Proper PPE
Time Required
- 10 Minutes
Procedure
- Put on proper PPE.
- Place the waste bottle on a counter top.
- Unscrew the bottle cap and place to the side.
- Visually look inside the bottle and make sure both, empty and full rotational floats are in.
- If either of one of the rotational floats are found broken, DO NOT use the bottle and order a replacement.
Verification
In the service Software, make sure the waste bottle empty/full sensor reads correctly.

## Waste Drawer Coalescing Trap Upgrade
id="mc-main-content">
Waste Drawer Coalescing Trap Upgrade
Purpose
This procedure provides instructions on how to replace the existing filter and coalescing trap (if present).
What is Affected
Vacuum and waste drawer, existing filter (T8 or Odorcarb) and coalescing trap (T8 Configuration) .
Parts and Materials Required
- Proper Protective Equipment
- FSE Toolkit
- FILTER (BLEACH), ODORCARB, 0.2UM CARTRIDGE
- WASTE DWR, COALESCING TRAP, GAC, UPGRADE KIT
Time Required
- 60 Minutes
Procedure
-
Shut down the Panther GUI, Panther System, and PC. Turn off the main power.
-
Open the waste drawer and properly dispose of the solid waste bag and waste cover.
-
Remove the waste bottle and the front cover of the Waste Drawer.
-
If upgrading a T8 with Coalescing Trap configuration:
-
Refer to Odorcarb Vacuum Filter Upgrade Procedure Steps 1-4 to remove the T8 filter and Steps 7-8 to remove the coalescing trap .
-
Continue to Step 6.
-
If upgrading a GAC filter configuration:
-
Remove the current GAC filter from the quick connect fittings (top and bottom of filter) and discard.
-
Remove the elbow fitting and extension tube that was connected to the bottom of the filter .
-
Remove the quick connect fitting from the vacuum tube . If the tubing requires cutting to remove the fitting, cut as close to the fitting as possible.
-
Use an 8mm wrench or socket to remove the two nuts and tubing clamps that secure the tubing to the side wall. Loosely reinstall the nuts on the posts and discard the tubing clamp s.
-
Attach the elbow fitting from the kit, to the vacuum tube (reuse the existing elbow if upgrading from a T8 configuration) .
-
Insert the new coalescing trap by routing the long tubing near the front of the system. As you seat the trap, guide the short tubing onto the barbed fitting .
Note— Verify all tubing is NOT kinked or pinched.
-
Install the two screws from the kit into the front and rear mounting holes under the drawer in the original location where the coalescing trap was installed.
-
Install the trap holder onto the posts and tighten the nuts .
-
Grease the O-rings on both ends of the filter and install the filter .
-
Install the quick connect fitting onto the tubing that has been provided in the kit .
-
Install the quick connect fitting with tubing onto the filter. Cut the tubing to reach the elbow fitting on the vacuum tube. Connect the tubing to the elbow of the vacuum tubing in the waste drawer.
-
Reinstall the Waste Drawer front cover, Waste Bottle, and waste bag with the cover.
Verification
-
Verify the Waste Drawer opens and closes smoothly.
-
Use Service Software to monitor the Panther Vacuum pressure. After 5 to 10 minutes the Panther Vacuum pressure should settle into a range of 6 and 8 in Hg (-203 and -271 mbar).
-
Verify the system successfully passes Prime Operation of pumping fluid through tubing to ensure proper and consistent fluid delivery (remove air from the tubing, etc.). .

## Draining the Coalescing Trap Procedure
id="mc-main-content">
Draining the Coalescing Trap Procedure
Parts and Materials Required
- Proper PPE
- Flat tray to catch fluid
- Allen wrench, 8 mm
Time Required
- 10 minutes
Removal Procedure
- Put on proper PPE .
- Open the Waste Drawer.
- Locate the coalescing drain plug on the right side of the Waste Drawer .
- Place a flat tray underneath the coalescing drain plug to catch any fluid that drains out.
- Using an 8 mm Allen wrench, slowly open the coalescing drain plug .
- After all fluid has drained, close the coalescing drain plug .
- Properly dispose of the liquid waste fluid from the drain.
- Clean the areas with bleach/water/alcohol that fluid from the trap came into contact with.
- Properly dispose of gloves.

## Odorcarb Vacuum Filter Upgrade Procedure
id="mc-main-content">
Odorcarb Vacuum Filter Upgrade Procedure
Do NOT upgrade a T8 filter to the Odorcarb filter, until directed.
Parts and Materials Required
- Proper PPE
- Panther Tool Kit
To replace the filter only:
- Filter, Odorcarb Refill, 0.2um Cartridge
The Odorcarb filter MUST be replaced every 12 months (from the date of install).
To upgrade to the new Odorcarb Filter:
- OdorCarb Filter Retrofit Kit
- 2 – Quick Connect Fittings
- 1 – 36” Extension Tube
- 1 – 90° Plastic Elbow Fitting
- 3 – Zip Ties
Time Required
- 1 hour to upgrade from T8 to Odorcarb Filter
Procedure
Caution—Perform this section only if the new Odorcarb Filter and Retrofit Kit are not installed.
- Shut down the Panther GUI, Panther System and PC. Turn off main power.
- Open the Waste Drawer, and properly dispose of the waste drawer cover & solid waste bag.
- Empty the Liquid Waste Bottle and set aside.
Note— If the old Waste Bottle male couplings (grey) are still installed, install the new CPC Couplings (white). Refer to Waste Bottle Male Fitting Upgrade .
- Remove & discard the T8 Vacuum Filter by disconnecting the upper tubing connector from its elbow fitting and the lower tubing connector from the Coalescing Bottle . Discard the T8 Filter. Ensure local laws and regulations are adhered to when disposing of the Vacuum Filter.
- Using a tubing cutter (or utility knife), remove the old elbow fitting from the vacuum tubing by cutting the tubing as close to the end of the elbow fitting as possible.
Note— If too much tubing is removed it will be too short to accommodate the new filter.
- Insert a quick-connect fitting (from the Filter retrofit kit) onto the end of the newly cut vacuum tubing. This is now the TOP  quick-connect.
- Unscrew the three Philips screws on the bottom of the Waste Drawer , just below the Coalescing Drain Plug, to free the Coalescing Bottle.
Note— The three Philips screws can be removed using a Chapman driver tool set or similar tool without removing the Waste Drawer from the rails. (The image on the right below shows the drawer removed for illustration purposes only.)
- Pull the Coalescing Bottle off its vacuum tube fitting. Remove the Coalescing Bottle from the drawer and discard it. Ensure local laws and regulations are adhered to when disposing of the Coalescing Bottle.
- Take a plastic elbow and extension tube from the retrofit kit and insert one end of the elbow into the extension tube .
- Attach the extension tube to the vacuum tube exiting the liquid waste bottle (the tube that was previously connected to the bottom of the coalescing bottle).
Note— If the end of the vacuum tube has an angled cut on the end, use the tubing cutter or utility knife to make a straight cut so the tube fits securely on the plastic elbow.
- Zip tie the two tubes loosely together in the bottom corner of the waste drawer .
- Ensure the new elbow fitting is positioned so that both tubes connected to it are flat against the bottom of the drawer and the elbow is next to the dividing wall.
- This may require pushing excess tubing back towards the Liquid Waste Bottle side.
- Pull the other tube upwards to provide as much extra tubing as possible for the TOP quick-connect Filter (Top of the OdorCarb Filter). Be sure not to put excessive tension on the tubing.
- Once this has been done securely tighten the zip tie.
- Attach a quick-connect (from the retrofit kit) to the other end of the extension tube. This is now the Bottom quick-connect.
- Connect the bottom of the new OdorCarb filter to the extension tube .
Verify arrows on the filter are pointing UP .
- Connect the top of the new filter to the Top quick-connect on the other vacuum tube . Slide the new connected filter into the drawer.
- Route the extension tube in a loop from the new plastic elbow in the bottom corner, up and around the new filter, and back down underneath. The illustration and images below show the best way to route the extension tube.
Note— The extension tube loop should be placed so that there is a minimum of stress, bending, sharp corners or twists of the tube to ensure proper operation of the vacuum system.
- Reseat the Liquid Waste Bottle.
- Install a new Solid Waste bag & Waste Drawer Cover.
- Close the Waste Drawer.
Verification
- From Panther Service Software:
- Verify vacuum levels are within specification.
[ -203mBar (6inHg) to -270mBar (8 inHg)]
- Verify that the Waste Drawer Full and Empty sensors work.
- Verify the Waste Drawer closes, latches and locks correctly.
- From Panther GUI software, successfully complete a full Prime Operation of pumping fluid through tubing to ensure proper and consistent fluid delivery (remove air from the tubing, etc.). .

## Tapping the Waste Bottle Mounting Block
id="mc-main-content">
Tapping the Waste Bottle Mounting Block
Purpose
To provide service personnel with a step-by-step procedure to enlarge and re-thread the waste bottle mounting block holes to accommodate the Polysulfone CPC male fittings on Panther Systems with serial numbers less than 674.
What is Affected
The waste bottle mounting block on systems with serial numbers less than 674 were threaded to accommodate the Polypropylene CPC connector [PN 900578, Insert, 3/8 NPT-M]. A more reliable Polysulfone CPC fitting [MME-02058, Coupling, Panther, waste bottle CPC] was released for upgrade but it is difficult to thread into the preexisting holes. In this procedure we introduce a tap tool needed to enlarge and re-thread the holes and provide instructions on the adjustment of the waste bottle mounting block.
Please reference Replace the Two Male Fittings in the Waste Drawer that Connect to the Waste Bottle .
Parts and Materials Required
- Proper PPE
- Adjustable Wrench
- Dow Corning High Vacuum Grease
- 4 mm Allen Wrench
- PANTHER, KIT, WASTE FITTING 3/8 IN NPT TAP
- 2x COUPLING, PANTHER, WASTE BOTTLE CPC
Time Required
- 25 Minutes
Procedure
- Put on proper PPE.
- Power down the Panther System.
- Open the waste drawer.
- Remove the liquid waste bottle.
- Clean the waste block seat and CPC fittings with a towel soaked in 10% bleach.
- Wait 10 minutes and remove the bleach from the surfaces with a disposable towel.
- Remove the 2 CPC male fittings from the waste bottle mounting block with an adjustable wrench.
- Use a PANTHER, KIT, WASTE FITTING 3/8 IN NPT TAP to re-thread the existing holes in the waste bottle seat block following the steps below:
- Slowly rotate the tap into the hole clockwise using only your fingers.
Caution—Do not cross-thread the tap in the hole.
- Once the tap can no longer be threaded by hand, use an adjustable wrench to continue tapping the hole.
- Progress with tapping the hole by rotating the tap ¼ turn clockwise then ¼ turn counterclockwise followed by a ¼ turn clockwise.
- Repeat the step above until the tap bottoms out in the hole; this should correlate with 2 threads on the top of the tap exposed above the waste bottle seat block.
- Once the tap is fully seated, remove the tap by rotating it counterclockwise while cleaning any filings that were produced during the tapping process.
- Clean any filings that may have been left behind in the tapped hole.
- Repeat the steps above on the second hole in the waste bottle mounting block.
- Hand thread the 2 new polysulfone CPC fittings into the waste bottle mounting block.
- Tighten the CPC fittings with an adjustable wrench until the fittings are fully seated.
- Once the 2 CPC fittings are in place apply a thin layer of vacuum grease to the black o-rings on the fittings.
- Adjust the height of the waste block seat.
- Loosen the 2 bolts on the side of the waste drawer with a 4mm Allen Wrench shown in the image below.
- With the bolts loose lift the waste bottle mounting block up as high as it will travel and tighten the 2 bolts loosened in the previous step.
- Fully seat the waste bottle in the waste drawer.
- Loosen the bolts on the side of the waste drawer shown in step a and push down on the waste bottle.
- Allow the waste bottle to settle then fully tighten the bolts on the side of the waste drawer.
Verification
- Power on the Panther System.
- Open the Panther GUI.
- Monitor the vacuum pressure through the Panther GUI.
- After 5 minutes the Panther vacuum pressure should settle into a range of 7 in/Hg +/- 1 in/Hg.
- Verify that the system can successfully pass prime.

# Section: Software

## RD_SW_Check_Pro360 with RemoteDash
id="mc-main-content">
Checking PRO360° Remote Diagnostics Connectivity from the Panther Remote Dashboard
- Log in to the FSE Panther Shield
- Click the Dashboard button.
- The Panther Dashboard software launches.
- Select the PRO360° Connection Tester tab and click Execute Tests .
If all connections are established, all Results will be labeled Good with green backgrounds .
Note— If a connection was not established, the Result will be labeled Bad with a red background .
- Close the Panther Dashboard software.

## Checking PRO360° Remote Diagnostics Connectivity with Technical Support
id="mc-main-content">
Checking PRO360° Remote Diagnostics Connectivity with Technical Support
Parts and Materials Required
- Panther System PC Workstation
Time Required
- 20 minutes
Procedure
- Launch the Panther System main assay software and log in as an Admin User .
- Confirm that the Panther System is not in Assay Procedures required to prepare and perform a specific test. In the context of this document, assay refers exclusively to a Hologic test, such as Aptima Combo or Ultrio. Processing mode .
Note— If the Panther System is in Assay Processing mode, wait until the system enters any state other than Assay Processing before proceeding.
- On the FSE laptop, click the PRO360° desktop icon to open a new session.
- Create a Session Code :
- Click Session Assignment .
- Enter the Panther System Serial Number in the Customer Code field.
- Click Create Code .
A Session Code appears on the screen .
- On the Panther System, navigate to the Messages tab and click the button at the bottom of button.
A Remote Diagnostics Management dialog box appears .
- Press Start .
A PRO360° popup window appears.
- Enter the newly generated Session Code and select Accept .
Note— If an incorrect Session Code is entered, a warning will appear, indicating "session not found," followed by a prompt to enter a correct Session Code.
At this point you can access the Panther System through the FSE laptop.
- Ensure that the File Transfer Control checkbox under Advanced Settings is checked (it is checked by default).
- If the Advanced Settings drop-down is not visible, click the + sign to see the settings .
- Click Control the Customer's Computer and ensure that the True Color option is selected .
- Click Launch Remote Control to view the Panther System screen on the FSE laptop .
You can now control over the Panther System and can navigate to different screens .
- Click the Tools button to access the File Transfer on the drop-down menu .
A File Explorer screen appears.
- Transfer log files from the Panther System C: drive to a folder on the FSE laptop.
In the following example, the FSE laptop files appear in the upper half of the screen. The Panther System files appear in the lower section .
A File Transfer popup window indicates the progress of the transfer .
When the transfer is complete, the transferred file appears in the FSE laptop directory .
- To terminate the session, either close the PRO360° Remote Diagnostics application on the FSE laptop or select Cancel in the PRO360° popup window.

## Disabling the PRO360° Remote Diagnostics on the Panther System
id="mc-main-content">
Disabling the PRO360° Remote Diagnostics on the Panther System
Parts and Materials Required
- Panther PC Workstation
Time Required
- 10 minutes
Procedure
- Launch the Panther System main assay software and log in as an Admin User .
- Select the Admin button .
- Select the System Configuration button .
- Select the User Interface drop-down menu .
- Clear the Enable Remote Diagnostics check box .
- Select the Save button at the bottom of the screen .

## Enabling the PRO360° Remote Diagnostics on the Panther System
id="mc-main-content">
Enabling the PRO360° Remote Diagnostics on the Panther System
Parts and Materials Required
- Panther System PC Workstation
Time Required
- 10 minutes
Procedure
- Launch the Panther System main assay software and log in as an Admin User .
- Press the Admin button .
- Select the System Configuration button .
- Select the User Interface drop-down menu .
- Check Enable Remote Diagnostics .
- Select the Save button at the bottom of the screen .
Note—NEVER perform electromechanical operations while connected remotely to the Panther Instrument.

## Firewall Wizard v5xxxx
id="mc-main-content">
Firewall Wizard v5xxxx
Scope
This section provides instructions for installing the PRO360° Remote Diagnostics Remote Diagnostics hardware and software.
Parts and Materials Required
- Completed AW-19118 Panther / Panther Scalable Solutions and Panther Fusion Site Assessment
- Firewall Kit
- Cisco Firewall ASA 5505 (1)
- Ac/DC Power Supply Adapter (1)
- 110V UPS Power Cable (1)
- Network Ethernet Cables (2)
- Serial Cable (1)
- Firewall Power Supply-to-UPS or PDU Cable (depends on the UPS in use: 110V vs 220V)
- Firewall Wizard Software CD
- For Panther System 220V UPS or PDU, 220V UPS Cable
- USB-to-Serial Adapter Cable (for use on FSE/ISE Service Laptops with USB Ports instead of Serial Ports)
- FSE/ISE Service Laptop running Microsoft Windows XP or 7 Operating System
- Network Ethernet Cables
Time Required
- 30 minutes (as long as the Panther System Site Assessment Form contains complete and accurate networking information)
Procedure
I. Installing the Firewall Wizard Software
This section describes how to install the Firewall Wizard Software. If it is already installed on the Service Laptop, skip to the next section, II. Configuring the Firewall.
- Close all applications running on the Service Laptop.
- Insert the Firewall Wizard Installation CD.
- If the Installation Program does not start automatically, navigate to the CD and double click the folder named Wizard X.X.X.X , then double-click the FirewallWizard file.
- Accept all default suggestions by clicking Next on each screen and install the software.
- When the installation is complete, verify that the desktop contains an icon labeled FirewallWizard X.X.X.X , where X.X.X.X is the current software version number.
- Double-click the Wizard icon and verify that the software starts and displays the Welcome to the Gen-Probe Firewall Configuration Wizard page.
II. Configuring the Firewall
This section describes how to custom configure the Firewall using network information supplied in the Network Configuration section of the Panther System Site Assessment Form.
A. Connecting the Firewall to the Laptop
- Turn on the laptop and wait for the Operating System (XP or 7) to start.
- Remove all cables from the Firewall.
- Plug the Firewall AC Alternating current /CD Power Supply Adapter into the Firewall jack marked Power.
- Plug the appropriate Firewall Power UPS Cable into the AC/DC Adapter.
- Plug the Firewall Serial Cable RJ45 connector into the Firewall jack marked Console.
- If equipped, plug the Firewall Serial Cable into the Service Laptop's RS-232/DB-9 Serial Port and skip to step 9.
- If the Service laptop does not have an RS-232/DB-9 connector, plug the Firewall Serial Cable (DB-9 connector) into the mating DB-9 connector of the USB-to-Serial Adapter Cable.
- Plug the USB connector into the Service Laptop.
- If the Microsoft Windows XP or 7 Operating system begins to install a driver, wait until the process finishes. Microsoft may try to install a driver for the USB device. If this occurs, see installation instructions in SOP 19-02-03 Installation of USB-to-Serial Converter Multi1USV RS232 XP PC.
B. Starting the Wizard Software
- On the Service Laptop desktop, double-click the Firewall Wizard icon.
The Welcome page appears.
- Ensure that the green Status light on the Firewall is on and steady for at least 60 seconds.
- Click Next on the Welcome to the Gen-Probe Firewall Configuration Wizard page to begin the data input process.
C. Selecting the Input Mode
Note— An existing configuration file can be loaded into the Wizard and can be used in the following situations:
- When completing a previous configuration attempt.
- When re-configuring the Firewall.
Starting with a New Configuration File
- To create and start with a new configuration file, select No on the Select how you want to enter information page and click Next .
- Continue to D. Selecting an Output Location.
Loading a Previously Saved Configuration File
- To load a previously saved configuration file, select Yes on the Select how you want to enter information page and click Next .
- Using the Open dialog box, navigate to the location of the previously saved configuration.
- Select the configuration file and click Open .
A File Load dialog appears.
- Click OK .
- Continue to D. Selecting an Output Location .
D. Saving Configuration Files
Configuration files can be stored to the default directory displayed on the Output Location page or to a new location.
Note— Configuration file descriptions are listed in Appendix A—Saved Configuration.
If Saving a Configuration File to the Default Directory
- Confirm that C:\Program Files\Gen-Probe\Firewall\Data displays in the text field and click Next .
- Continue to E. Configuring the FSE Laptop Serial Port.
If Saving a Configuration File to a Location Other than the Default Directory
- On the Select the folder to be used for saving output files page, click Change .
A Browse for Folder dialog appears.
- Navigate to the desired location for the configuration file.
- Click OK to confirm the new location or click Cancel to keep the default file location.
- Click Next .
- Continue to E. Configuring the FSE Laptop Serial Port .
E. Setting the FSE Laptop Serial Port Configuration for Communicating with the Firewall
When the Service Laptop is connected to the Firewall, the Wizard Serial Port page will verify and test the connection automatically.
- On the Serial Port page, the Wizard automatically displays the correct connected serial port. If another serial port is required, select the new serial port from the Port drop-down menu.
Testing Connection to COMx displays while the Wizard tests the connection.
Connect OK, IOS=x, ASDM=x displays when the test is complete.
- If there are no issues, click Next to continue to F. Setting Site and Instrument Information .
- If No connected ports displays, check to be sure the cables are connected.
- Click Test to test the connection.
- When the connection is confirmed, continue to F. Setting Site and Instrument Information .
F. Setting Site and Instrument Information
This section provides the configuration output files with the default filenames for ease of retrieval. This section also allows the FSE/ISE to select which Instrument type with which the Firewall will be used. This information can be found in the Panther System Site Assessment Form.
Note— Entries into the Site Info page text boxes are limited to 35 alpha/numeric characters and spaces.
- On the Site Info page, enter the following information:
-
Site Name
-
FSE/ISE full name
-
Firewall Serial Number (the serial number is located on the back of the firewall component)
- Select Panther for the Gen-Probe Instrument Model and click Next .
G. Configuring the Firewall for Instrument Environment (Customer Site vs. Gen-Probe Internal)
The Wizard can configure the Firewall to communicate with a Customer Site or with an internal Gen-Probe Development Environment.
Note— Customer Site is the default setting for FSE installs.
If the Firewall will be used at a Customer Site
- On the Specify where the Firewall is physically Located page, select Yes and click Next .
- Continue to H. Entering IP Address Settings .
If the Firewall will be used at Gen-Probe
- On the Specify where the Firewall is physically Located page, select No, this is a special firewall inside Gen-Probe and click Next .
A Select Environments for Firewall Located inside Gen-Probe page appears.
- Select at least one of the following server environments:
- RDxM Production
- RDxM QAS / V and V
- RDxM Development
- Axeda Enterprise
- Axeda Sandbox
- Click Next .
H. Entering IP Address Settings
The Wizard can configure the Firewall to allow a customer's network to assign a temporary IP address (DHCP) or to assign a permanent IP address (Static IP Address). This information is contained in the Panther System Site Assessment Form.
For DHCP Addressing
- On the Select Dynamic or Static Outside Firewall IP Address page, select DHCP and click Next .
- On the Select how to specify the DHCP Range , select either Use IP Address Range or Use Gateway , according to the information on the Panther System Site Assessment Form, and click Next .
- If the customer site uses a DHCP IP Address Range, on the Outside Firewall DHCP IP Address Range page, enter the starting and ending IP Addresses and click Next .
- If the customer site uses a DHCP Gateway, enter the Gateway Address and click Next .
For Static IP Addressing
- On the Select Dynamic or Static Outside Firewall IP Address page, select Static IP Address and click Next .
- On the Network Configuration for the Static outside Firewall page, enter the Firewall, Netmask, and Gateway IP Addresses from the Panther System Site Assessment Form and click Next .
I. Entering DNS Settings
DNS must be configured on the Firewall, because the PRO360° NTR Global and the PRO360° RSL applications use domain names (i.e., RDxM.Gen-Probe.com) to access Gen-Probe servers. DNS allows this software to resolve these domain names to IP Addresses (i.e., RDxM.Gen-Probe.com resolves to 70.164.126.19).
The Preferred DNS IP and Alternate DNS IP will be pre-populated. Both DNS IP Address entries are required. The default values can be deleted and replaced with customer-selected values, if preferred. This information can be found in the Panther System Site Assessment form.
The Wizard requires two DNS IP non-duplicate addresses to be entered for configuring the Firewall. Any combination of default addresses and customer-selected values can be used to configure the Firewall.
- On the Enter the Domain Name Server (DNS) Addresses to be Used page, enter and confirm both DNS addresses.
- To reset to the default values, click Defaults .
- Click Next .
J. Connecting to a TCP/IP LIS
- For customers requesting Panther instrument communication to their LIS using a TCP/IP interface, select Yes and click Next .
- Enter the LIS Server IP address and TCP Port, and click Next .
K. Specifying a Network Printer
- For customers requesting networked printing services using the printers approved for the Panther System, select Yes and click Next .
L. Firewall Acceptance and Configuration
After all parameters have been entered into the Wizard, a Please Review Your Input page displays all entries.
- Verify that each entry on the page matches the information in the Network Configuration section of the Panther System Site Assessment Form .
- When satisfied that all information is correct, click Save .
A File Save dialog box appears.
- Click OK .
- Confirm that the Service Laptop is properly connected to the Firewall.
- On the Please Review Your Input page, click Configure .
A Configuring Firewall page appears, with a progress bar at the bottom of the page that indicates the percentage of completion.
Note— Do not run any other applications (such as email or Internet Explorer) while the configuration is in progress.
A Configuration Completed pop-up screen appears when all inputs have been accepted and the Firewall has been configured.
- Read the Configuration Completed pup-up screen and click OK .
- On the Configuration Successful page, click Exit .

## Connecting the Configured Firewall to the Panther System
id="mc-main-content">
Connecting the Configured Firewall to the Panther System
- Unplug the Serial Cable RJ45 connector from the Console port on the back of the Firewall.
- Unplug the other end of the Serial Cable and pack for future use.
- If used, unplug the USB-to-Serial Adapter Cable from the laptop and pack for future use.
- If the Firewall is not already in its operational location near the Panther System, plug the AC Alternating current /DC Power Supply Adapter into the Panther System UPS using the Power UPS/PDU cable.
- Connect the Firewall to the customer network.
- Plug one end of an Ethernet Cable (RJ45 connectors on each end) into the customer network (usually located on the wall).
- Plug the other end of the cable into Firewall Port 0 . The port number is located on the rear of the Firewall, on the yellow strip below the jack.
- Connect the Firewall to the Panther System.
- Plug one end of an Ethernet Cable (RJ45 connectors on each end) into Firewall Port 1 . The port number is located on the rear of the Firewall, on the yellow strip below the jack.
- Plug the other end of the cable into the Panther System PC NIC 1 Port .
- Verify proper installation by ensuring that the green LEDs are flashing for both Firewall network connections and the Panther System PC NIC 1 Port connection.

## Configuring the PC with a Static IP Address
id="mc-main-content">
Configuring the PC with a Static IP Address
Time Required
- 15 minutes
Prerequisite
- Programming the Firewall with Firewall Wizard v6.0.1.0
Procedure
- Upon PC boot up, touch the screen or press any key.
The Panther Shield software screen appears.
Note— If no key is pressed or the touch screen is not touched, the Panther System main assay software launches.
- Press Shift + F10 .
The FSE Password Login dialog box appears.
- Enter the following password:
!G9 x 53rvic3 y
Where x = the last digit of the day and y = the last digit of the month.
- Click OK .
The Panther FSE Shield software screen appears.
- Click the Command Prompt button.
- Enter control NCPA.CPL into the DOS Window and press Enter .
- Select the Local Area Connection that is currently enabled; the other connection should have a red X next to it .
- Position the mouse pointer over the enabled Local Area Connection , click the right mouse button, and select Properties .
- Select Internet Protocol Version 4 ( TCR Target capture reagent—An assay-specific reagent added as part of specimen pipetting. /IPv4) and click the Properties button .
Note— At this point, a dialog box appears requesting the IP address , Subnet mask , Default gateway , Preferred DNS server , and Alternate DNS server values.
- Select the Use the following IP address option
An Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) properties dialog box appears. .
- Enter the information from the Firewall Configuration Wizard Configuration Completed screen.
- After entering the information, click OK .
- Click Close .
- Close all open windows.
- Click the Start button in the lower left corner of the screen and select Restart .
- Checking PRO360° Remote Diagnostics Connectivity from the Panther Remote Dashboard

## Remote Service Link (RSL) Operational Qualification
id="mc-main-content">
Remote Service Link (RSL) Operational Qualification
This procedure entails testing RSL by performing a Send Logs packet and verifying it arrives on the correct EFT site.
Note—
For RSL to function correctly the last 5 digits of the System Serial Number MUST be recorded in the Panther GUI.
Parts and Materials Required
- Panther PC Workstation
- PC with EFT access
Time Required
- 10 minutes
Procedure
- Restart the system.
- Log in to the Panther System software with:
- Username: admin
- Password: pantherx
- Once the system reaches the Setup state, select the Messages button on the Menu Bar.
- Click the Send Logs button located near the bottom of the Messages screen.
- Click the Send to Service Support or the Send to Gen-Probe button.
- When prompted, click Yes to continue and wait for the operation to complete.
- Once the operation is completed, close the Panther System software.
- Log in to the Panther FSE Shield software.
- Open Windows Explorer.
- Navigate to the C:\panther\software\pc\bin\exporttogp directory.
- Verify there are no files inside the folder. If a Send Logs packet is still in the folder, wait 3 minutes and refresh the window.
- Login to the System's EFT site at eft.gen-probe.com.
- Username: user XXXXX
- Password: pw XXXXX
Where XXXXX is the Serial Number of the Panther System with leading 0s.
- Verify that the file is located on the EFT site.

## Remote Diagnostics Installation
id="mc-main-content">
Remote Diagnostics Installation
This section provides instructions for installing the PRO360° Remote Diagnostics hardware and software.
Note: NEVER perform any electromechanical operations while connected remotely to the Panther Instrument.
Installation Procedures
The procedures listed in the following table must be performed in sequential order:
- Programming the Firewall with the latest Firewall Wizard.
- Hardware Setup after Firewall has been configured
- Cisco 5506 ASA
- Cisco 5505 ASA
- Setting a Panther IP Address on the Panther Workstation
OR
Configuring the PC with a Static IP Address
- Enabling the PRO360° Remote Diagnostics on the Panther System
- Checking PRO360° Remote Diagnostics Connectivity from the Panther Remote Dashboard
- Checking PRO360° Remote Diagnostics Connectivity with Technical Support
- Disabling the PRO360° Remote Diagnostics on the Panther System (Only if requested by customer)

## Common Features
id="mc-main-content">
Common Features
Common Control
Each main screen in Service Software has a Common Control area that contains the following functions:
Initialize
Initialize any single module or all modules, depending on the selection in the Module dialog window.
Module dropdown
Select all modules, Dialog Controlled Modules only, or a single module.
Get Module Firmware
Displays the firmware version of the selected module.
Get Module Status
Displays the status (Initialized, Not Initialized, Ready, Not Ready) of the selected module.
Communication Status
Displays the communication status with the Panther COP (ok and idle, not initialized, etc.).
Buttons
Setup Report Header Data
Enter serial numbers, login name and customer information for report headers.
Driver Option
Setup driver options.
Exit
Closes service software.

## SC-Cartridge Tab
id="mc-main-content">
SC-Cartridge Tab
Refer to Common Features for features found on every tab (Common Control, Communication Status, Buttons).
Main (tab)
Sensors
- Temperatures - Reads the temperatures at the Peltiers, the two Storage Carousels Upper (Air 1) and Lower (Air 2), and the Ambient temp. The Peltiers and the Storage Carousels normally read slightly less than 15°C.
- Sensors - Displays the current status of listed sensors (LB is light barrier).
- Power Supply - Displays current voltage readings at the listed components.
Actors
- Cartridge Drawer - Manually lock or unlock the Cartridge Drawer (status is indicated by LED light).
- Fan - Manually control the two exterior fans. (These are visible when the front cover is removed.) Also control the interior fan (but not visible.)
- Peltier - Manually control each of the two Peltiers.
Cooling
- Temperatures - Reads the temperatures at the Peltiers, the two Storage Carousels Upper (Air 1) and Lower (Air 2), the Ambient Temp. and the Seebeck components. The Peltiers, Storage Carousels and Seebecks normally read slightly less than 15°C.
- Cooling Control - Manual control of the Cooling System. (Fans, Peltiers, thermistors.)
Move
- Carousel Init - Initialize the Loader or the Storage Carousel.
- Unload
- Inventory Button - Rotary Distributor checks all cartridge storage positions and generates a report listing each cartridge in storage.
- Unload to Loading Carousel - Moves all cartridges in storage to the loader.
- Unload Carousel to Waste - Moves all cartridges to waste.
- Loader - Moves the selected Loader Carousel slot (1-14) to either the Loading Position or Scan Position. The Start Continuous button moves the loader carousel continuously.
- Storage - Moves the selected Storage Carousel slot (1-14) to the Loading Position. The Start Continuous button moves the storage carousel continuously.
- Random Move - Generates continuous random movement of the Loader or Storage carousel.
Barcode
- Init - Initialize the Barcode Scanner or the Loading Carousel.
- Move/Scan - Move the selected cartridge to the Scan position and then Read the barcode.
- Scanner - Scan all positions or calibrate the scanner.
Module Info
- Cartridge Carousel - Displays Carousel information.
Parameter (tab)
- Display any parameter value of the selected Device by entering a Parameter number and clicking the Read button.
Error Memory (tab)
- Lists errors created by module movement.

## SC-Centrifuge
id="mc-main-content">
SC-Centrifuge
Refer to Common Features for features found on every tab (Common Control, Communication Status, Buttons).
Main (tab)
Sensors / Actors
- Sensors - Click Read to display the current state of the listed sensors.
- Load/Unload Light Barrier - Initiates a short test (with instructional prompts) to test the functionality of the Light Barriers.
Move
- Define Centrifuge Profile - Create a custom test profile to evaluate Centrifuge performance.
- Move - Select a loaded profile and click Start Centrifugation to evaluate the Centrifuge under the specific parameters in the profile. This is helpful to troubleshoot when there are failures during assay processing.
- Target Position dropdown - Move a selected centrifuge bucket to the Load or Unload position. This can help diagnose a Cap & Vial Presence failure.
Parameter (tab)
- Display any parameter value of the selected Device by entering a Parameter number and clicking the Read button.
Teach (tab)
- Not currently used for routine maintenance. Offsets are preloaded.
Error Memory (tab)
- Lists errors created by module movement.

## SC-Front and Loading Units Tab
id="mc-main-content">
SC-Front and Loading Units Tab
Refer to Common Features for features found on every tab (Common Control, Communication Status, Buttons).
Main (tab)
Drawer Interlocks
- Drawer Sensor - Reads current sensor states.
- Drawer Interlock - Reads current Drawer Interlock states (displays Locked/Unlocked).
- Drawer Interlock - Manually Lock and Unlock each drawer to test the functionality of the interlocks.
Elution Track
- Track Motor - Initialize the Elution Track Motor on the Universal Fluid Drawer, and move the Elution Arm over to the Panther side and back.
- Voltages - Read voltages at various components of the Fluid Drawer.
Cap & Vial RFID
- TAG Check - Test the sensors that read Cap & Vial tray information of trays inserted in positions 1,2,3,4.
Shutter
- Init Shutters button - Initialize the shutters
- Close All button - Closes the shutters.
- Check Position button - Checks the current position of the shutters.
- Select Column to Open - Opens the shutters over the selected Column and Tray (Left/Right).
- Motor Sensors - Indicates the current position of the motor (Home or Out).
Fluid Drawer LED
- LED - Tests LEDs to ensure lights are working properly.
Fluid Drawer RFID
- TAG Check - Reads and displays all the information on each TAG label for the selected position (Elution 1&2, Oil 1&2, Recon 1-4).
Front Cover
- Sensors - Reads current supply voltages/state/status of listed sensors.
- LEDs - Turn on/off or test any of the LED lights on the Front Panel.
- Waste - Manually Lock/Unlock the Waste Drawer. Can be used to calibrate a newly installed Drawer sensor.
- Fan - Manually check operation of the cooling fan.
Module Info
- Displays module information for displayed modules.
Teach Shutter (tab)
- To perform Shutter Teaching, refer to the Reaction Tube Tray Shutter Teaching Procedure .
Parameter (tab)
- Display any parameter value of the selected Device by entering a Parameter number and clicking the Read button.
- To allow Shutter teaching (on the Teach Shutter tab) the Authorization Code must be set to 1. Enter 1 in the Authorization Code Field and click Set before teaching.
Error Memory (tab)
- Lists errors created by module movement.

## SC-Pipettor Tab
id="mc-main-content">
SC-Pipettor Tab
Refer to Common Features for features found on every tab (Common Control, Communication Status, Buttons).
Main (tab)
XY - Random Movement
- Use when troubleshooting lost X or Y-axis steps, or after replacing X or Y-axis belts.
Sensors
- Vial Robot (Read button checks voltages on PCB, voltages out of range can indicate defects.)
- Reagent Pipettor (Read button checks voltages on PCB, voltages out of range can indicate defects. Also, LLD Frequency can indicate if wet. A value of 24000 Hz indicates wetness.)
Misc
- Not currently used.
Pumps
- Vial Robot (Initialize.)
- Reagent Pipettor (Initialize.)
Module Info
- Pipettor Main CU PCB (Displays info)
Move (tab)
- Vial Robot (Select location to move Vial Robot)
- Select Coordinate (Double-click from displayed list to send arm to selected Coordinates.)
- Reagent Pipettor (Select location to move Vial Robot)
- Move Sequence (Setup a pre-programmed move sequence)
- Check Record box.
- Single-click desired coordinate to add to list, double-click to add to list and preview the movement.
- Uncheck Record box.
- Edit the Sequence order if desired using Up, Down, Delete.
- Click Execute to start Sequence.
Caution—DO NOT allow arms to cross as there is no verification performed by the software.
LLD Reagent (Fusion) Pipettor (tab)
- Setup an LLD test on the Fusion Pipettor:
- Initialize the Fusion Pipettor.
- Double-click a location to add to Coord. List (PCR Recon Standard represents the Reconstitution Buffer positions 1-4 in the UFD, the PCR Recon LDT represents the PCR cartridge positions in the Reagent Aspiration Station, and Oil represents the A and B positions for Oil in the UFD.
- Enter desired number of cycles.
- Select Barometric (bar.) or Capacitive (cap.)
- Choose a "pierce" option.
- Check Log and click Execute to start test.
Parameter (tab)
- Display any parameter value of the selected Device by entering a Parameter number and clicking the Read button.
- Some parameters can be changed using file operations and saving to NVM.

## SC-Rotary Tab
id="mc-main-content">
SC-Rotary Tab
Refer to Common Features for features found on every tab (Common Control, Communication Status, Buttons).
Main (tab)
Handoff
- Handoff Station - Initializes only the Handoff Station submodule. Use the Move To buttons to rotate the Handoff Station to either the Linear or Rotary Distributor.
Sensors
- Home & MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station. Sensor - Displays current sensor state to aid troubleshooting.
- Power Supply - Displays current voltage read at each power supply.
- Oscillator - Used to test the current frequency measurement of the Oscillator. The Oscillator is only used during the Teaching process.
- Teach Sensor - Reads the current state frequency of the teach sensor.
Module Info
- Displays information on listed components.
Move (tab)
- Distributor Single Movement To - A single-click moves the Rotary Distributor to the selected location. A double-click will pick or place at the selected location.
- Distributor Repetition Movement - Create a custom series of repetitive movements to test operation.
Parameter (tab)
- Display any parameter value of the selected Device by entering a Parameter number and clicking the Read button.
- To allow Rotary Distributor teaching (on the Teach tab) the Authorization Code must be set to 1. Enter 1 in the Authorization Code Field and click Set before teaching.
Teach (tab)
- For Rotary Distributor teaching instructions, refer to the Teach Rotary Distributor to All Stations procedure.
- For Handoff Station teaching instructions, refer to the Teach Handoff Station to Linear Distributor procedure.
Error Memory (tab)
- Lists errors created by module movement.

## SC-System Tab
id="mc-main-content">
SC-System Tab
Refer to Common Features for features found on every tab (Common Control, Communication Status, Buttons).
SC-System (tab)
OQ-Test (tab)
- Initialize SC-System - Initializes the Side Car modules. Also have options to clear consumables from various modules.
- Side Car Pipettor OQ Test - Perform an operational check of the Pipettor functionality.
For instructions to perform a Side Car Pipettor OQ Test, refer to the Side Car Pipettor OQ Test procedure.
- Side Car System OQ Test - During this test, the Rotary Distributor will pick and place one MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station. or one PCR cartridge in every location in the system. If Elution Bottle is selected, the Elution Arm movement is tested.
The test procedure for this OQ is the same as the Panther Fusion System OQ Test.
For instructions to perform a Panther Fusion System OQ Test, refer to the Panther Fusion System OQ Test procedure.
- Pressure Integrity Test - Test pipettor pressure integrity.
For instructions to perform a Side Car Pressure Integrity Test, refer to the Fusion Pipettor Pressure Integrity Test procedure.
Parameter (tab)
- Display any parameter value of the selected Device by entering a Parameter number and clicking the Read button.

## SC-Thermocycler Tab
id="mc-main-content">
SC-Thermocycler Tab
Refer to Common Features for features found on every tab (Common Control, Communication Status, Buttons).
Main (tab)
TC-States
- Heatsink Sensors - Reads the temperature at each Thermistor. Thermistor 1 measures temperature under Banks 1-6, and Thermistor 2 measures temperature under Banks 7-12. Any differences in temperature readings can indicate a faulty thermistor.
- Actors - Manually turn the fans inside the Thermocycler on and off.
- TC States - Not used.
Bank Operations
- Bank Operations - not currently in use.
Sequence
- Select Bank - Runs a stress test on selected Banks.
- Graph - Displays a graph of florescent data for selected fluorometers.
Cleaning (tab)
- Reserved for future use.
Scan Results (tab)
This tab is used to evaluate all the banks for potentially "dirty/blocked" wells.
Scan Background (used with a PEEK lid up, or no PEEK lid present)
- Enter a value for BGMax. (BGMax is a limit that will flag a “dirty” well, some value above 1. The default is 1.8, meaning locations with an average reading of more than 80% of the median found from all wells will get flagged.)
- Click the Scan Background button.
- The “Well – Average values” and “Fluorometer – Median Values” tables will show results. "Dirty/blocked" locations will be highlighted in yellow.
Scan PEEK Lid (used only with a PEEK lid down and covering the banks)
- Scan the barcode on the PEEK lid, or manually enter PEEK lid values.
- Enter values for LEDMin and PEEKMin to set evaluation criteria. (0.7 and 0.6 are default – if locations have average readings less than these, the wells will be flagged or error notice will appear.)
- Click Scan PEEK Lid button.
- The “Well – Average values” and “Fluorometer – Median Values” tables will show results. "Dirty/blocked" locations will be highlighted. An error message, “LED Failure” is displayed if an LED has failed.
Parameter (tab)
- Display any parameter value of the selected Device by entering a Parameter number and clicking the Read button.
Error Memory (tab)
- Lists errors created by module movement.

## SC-X-Fusion Tab
id="mc-main-content">
SC-X-Fusion Tab
Refer to Common Features for features found on every tab (Communication Status, Buttons).
Fusion - Test (tab)
- Initialize System - Initializes the entire Panther Fusion System. Also have options to clear consumables.
- Fusion Transfer Test - This test verifies successful transfer of an MTU Multi-tube unit—Container used to process tests in the instrument. An MTU contains five separate reaction tubes. The MTU is moved through the instrument by the linear distributor and includes five tiplets for pipettiing to be used in the mag wash station. to the Fusion and back to the Panther.
For instructions to perform a Fusion Transfer Test, refer to the Fusion Transfer Test procedure.
- System OQ Test - During this test, the Rotary Distributor will pick and place one MTU or one PCR cartridge in every location in the system. If Elution Bottle is selected, the Elution Arm movement is tested.
For instructions to perform a System OQ Test, refer to the Panther Fusion System OQ Test procedure.
Fusion - Handoff Station Teach (tab)
- Initialize LD Linear distributor /ROT System - Initializes the Linear Distributor and Rotary Distributor for teaching.
- For instructions to teach the handoff station to the Linear Distributor, refer to the Teach Handoff Station to Linear Distributor procedure.

## Network Configuration
id="mc-main-content">
Network Configuration
Note— Prior to setting up any Network connections, the Networking section of the Panther Site Assessment Form MUST be completed.
Panther Link requires the following:
- Dell XE3
- System SW v7.1.5.4 and above
- Cisco 5506 Firewall
- Firewall Wizard v6.0.1.0 and above
If a Panther is connected to an external (customer) network, that Panther MUST have a firewall installed.
There are 2 types of Firewalls currently supported:
- Cisco ASA 5505
- Cisco ASA 5506
Both firewalls will be programed with the latest Firewall Wizard.
After the Firewall is programed using the Firewall Wizard, an instructions.txt file will be generated to guide the installation of all hardware.
The instructions.txt file will aid in setting up the IP addresses for all Panther Instruments, the WMS, Line Controller and Dashboard Server.
Follow the steps outlined below to network a Panther (or multiple Panthers).
- Download and install the latest Firewall Wizard.
- Connect the Cisco ASA 5505/5506 to FSE Laptop
- Programming the Firewall with the latest Firewall Wizard.
- Hardware Setup after Firewall has been configured
- Cisco 5506 ASA
- Cisco 5505 ASA
- Setting a Panther IP Address on the Panther PC
- Network Printing (if required)
- Panther LINK Installation Qualification
Note: If this is an install, continue to Operational Qualifiation (OQ) .

## Using the Panther System Service Manual
id="mc-main-content">
Using the Panther System Service Manual
Service Manual Screen Layout
The Panther Service Manual uses a standard WebHelp layout to organize and present information. The screen is divided into three major sections—the side navigation, the top toolbar, and content pane .
Side Navigation
The navigation pane is located on the left side of the screen and provides quick access to the different topics available in the service manual. To open one of the topics click on the title listed.
Top Toolbar
The top toolbar contains the following icons that help you locate information in the service manual.
Toolbar Icon
Description
Print —Press to print the topic currently displayed in the content pane.
Collapse All —Press to collapse all image and text togglers on a topic page.
Expand All —Press to display all image and text togglers on a topic page.
Feedback —Press to send feedback, comments, or change request to the Service Manual team.
Content Pane
The content pane displays the currently selected service manual topic.

id="mc-main-content">

# Section: System

## CEE 7/7 Power Cords for European Systems
id="mc-main-content">
CEE 7/7 Power Cords for European Systems
What is Affected
There are no universal polarity standards for the Type E and Type F power sockets commonly used in Europe. Only the former Czechoslovakia had implemented a polarity standard for the Type E socket, requiring line (live) to be on the left side of the socket and neutral on the right (with the ground pin on top). Because of this, the orientation of the line and neutral slots on these types of sockets can vary from site to site.
The current Panther power cord released for use with these sockets, Gen-Probe P/N: 902700 (Supplier P/N: 8510.098) is configured with the line pin on the left and neutral pin on the right, when looking at the plug with the ground slot on top (see figure 3). The Panther UPS has an audible alarm which activates if plugged into a power socket with a polarity that does not match that of its power inlet. On the Type F (Schuko) sockets, this can be corrected by unplugging and rotating the plug 180 degrees, and then reinserting into the socket. However, the Type E (French) sockets will not allow the plug to be repositioned in this manner due to the presence of an off-centered, protruding ground pin (see figure 1). In these instances, a cord with the opposite polarity is required. Gen-Probe P/N: 903229 (Supplier P/N: 86230110) has been released, which has the opposite polarity of P/N: 902700 and follows the polarity standard set by the former Czechoslovakia (see figure 4).
The two power cords specified in this document can be used to connect the PANTHER uninterruptible power supply (UPS) or power distribution unit (PDU) to European Type E or Type F electrical sockets. Although both types sockets are found throughout Europe, Type E sockets (figure 1) are often used in (but not limited to) France, Belgium, Poland, Czech Republic, and Slovakia. Type F sockets are commonly found in (but not limited to) Germany, Austria, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, and some other Eastern European and Balkan countries.
Table1 lists the two approved power cords for use with the PANTHER UPS and PDU at sites using Type E or F electrical sockets. FSEs are responsible for determining and ordering the appropriate cord to use before systems installation or cord replacement.
Parts and Materials Required
- Non-contact Voltage Tester
Note— The Fluke VoltAlert non-contact voltage tester is used for the indication of hot (live/line) wires only. It does not measure voltage or current and does not require calibration.
Time Required
- 10 Minutes
Procedure
- Using a non-contact AC Alternating current voltage tester, determine the orientation of the line and neutral slots on the socket that the Panther UPS or PDU will be connected to:
- Turing the Tester On - Momentarily press the green button. Listen for a double beep to confirm activation. A continual Voltbeat flash visually indicates the Tester is active.
Note— Voltbeat is a self-test feature for visual confirmation of battery and system integrity, and power on. It provides a double-flash every two seconds during normal operation.
- Checking for the Presence of AC Voltage - Insert the tip of the tester into a slot on the power socket. If the tester produces a steady glow at the tip of the tester, and if enabled, a continual beep, then the slot contains live AC Voltage. If no glow and continual beep (if enabled) is produced by the tester, then there is no AC voltage in the slot. Test the other slot to determine if it contains AC Voltage. The slot with AC voltage is the line (live) slot. The opposite slot should not contain AC Voltage and is the neutral slot.
- Turning the Tester Off - Press and hold the green button for more than half a second. Listen for a long half second beep to confirm deactivation of the Tester. The absence of the VoltBeat flash indicates the Tester is inactive.
Note— Disabling the Beeper - The beeper can be disabled by holding the green button down for more than two seconds during power up. The absence of the VoltBeat flash indicates the Tester is inactive.
Note— Low Battery Indication - When the battery voltage drops below two volts, VoltBeat provides visual indication by stopping the Voltbeat flash. Replace with two AAA (LR3) batteries.
- Obtain the cord containing the plug with the line and neutral pin orientation that will match the line and neutral slots when plugged into the socker.
Note— When looking directly at the plug (pin towards you) with the ground slot at top, the orientation of the line and neutral pins will be opposite that of the line and neutral slots on the socket (when looking directly at the socket). When used for Type E sockets, ensure that the cord selected will contain line and neutral pins that will mate with the correct slots when it is plugged into the socket (see table 1 for reference). When used for Type F sockets, ensure that the cord’s plug is oriented correctly so that the pins will mate with the correct slots when plugged into the socket.
- Use the cord to connect the UPS or PDU to the socket.
Note— When connecting the UPS to an electrical socket, an audible alarm will activate if the polarity is incorrect. Either unplug and rotate the plug 180 degrees and reinsert to correct the orientation (for Type F sockets only) or change to the cord with the opposite polarity.
Note— PDUs will not alarm even if the polarity is incorrect, so ensure that the polarity of the cord matches that of the socket that it will be plugged into.

## Customer Confidentiality
id="mc-main-content">
Customer Confidentiality
It is our policy to ensure the confidentiality of our customer's information.
Service personnel should not use any customer information for any purpose other than providing customer service or disclose such information to third parties.
In particular, service personnel who access customer equipment, either directly or through remote tools, should ensure they are not provided access to personally identifiable medical or health information.
Such information may include information held by a customer that concerns health status, provision of health care, or payment for health care which can be linked to an individual.
If, in the course of providing customer service, service personnel inadvertently view or access any personally identifiable medical or health information, service personnel should treat such information as strictly confidential and should not disclose such information to any third party or use such information for any purpose.
We advise customers to use industry best practices regarding patient health information and do not recommend sending patient identifying information to instrumentation.

## Panther System Device Description
id="mc-main-content">
Panther System Device Description
The main components of the Panther System are the system and computer workstation. The computer workstation directs the system modules to perform the assay steps. The system houses all the computer, fluids, reagents, consumables, and mechanical modules to perform the assay. Optional accessories outside the system housing are, for example printers, firewall, and uninterruptible power supply. The system computer can accommodate LIS connectivity and remote user access.
The mechanical modules include a reagent pipettor probe, a sample pipettor probe, fluid delivery module (pumps and valves), reagent bay for loading reagent racks, sample bay for loading sample racks, a TCR Target capture reagent—An assay-specific reagent added as part of specimen pipetting. compartment containing Target Capture Reagent vessels, drawers for disposable tips, a Distributor, Input and Output queues for MTUs, two Magnetic Wash Stations, three Incubators, various mixers, Chiller Ramps, Parking Slots, a Luminometer, a compartment for the computer, a compartment for solid and liquid waste, a compartment for Universal Fluids, a liquid based Cooling Module, and a vacuum pump.
Each sample rack can hold 15 samples. Each reagent rack can accommodate the required assay specific reagents for an assay—AMP, enzyme, probe, and select (TCR are loaded independently). There are three rack sizes—100tk, 250tk, and 500tk. Barcode scanners are provided for the samples, reagents, and utilized for reaction tube identification, sample, and reagent tracking. An RFID system is used to track the universal fluids. The system software monitors the system status, reagent and supply inventories, test requests, test results, and maintenance. An internal vacuum system controls the aspiration of liquids from the magnetic wash station and output queue.

## Electro-Magnetic Compatibility
id="mc-main-content">
Electro-Magnetic Compatibility
The electrical design in the Panther system is developed to pass all electrical safety and electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements:
- A primary main filter is used in addition to the Power Supply primary filter to reduce conducted emission from the system and increase conducted immunity.
- The +24V power and CAN-bus connections between COP and CU PCBs are filtered with additional SMD-ferrites
- System Inputs and Outputs is protected by SMD filter and RC-networks
- All specific metal housing parts is connected to the base ground via a screwed connection. This is especially important for all user accessible modules, such as the load stations, to discharge possible static energy.
- PCBs that are assembled directly on a grounded metal sheet are electrical connected to that metal sheet by the PCB mounting screws.
- All CU PCBs are 4 layer PCBs, with one internal ground layer.
- The buried capacitance technology places the internal ground and the +5V layer close together, forming a very good high frequency capacitor to improve EMI.

## Fault Protection
id="mc-main-content">
Fault Protection
Each CU PCB is able to monitor the +24V input voltage for over and under voltage detection and signals the status to the COP.
Each +24V output driver IC for a DC-pump, DC-motor or a heat foil has a diagnose function, to signal a possible “Open Load” condition to the respective processor at that CU PCB.
The Pipettor Module CU PCB is able to switch independently the motor power of the left and right X-, Y- and Z-motor ON and OFF. The PIP CU processor is able to switch off the motor power in case of emergency (crash or jam).
The Cooling CU PCB and Chiller Ramp CU PCB monitor the Setback voltage of the Peltier devices so a fault can be detected.

## Instrument Fluidic Management
id="mc-main-content">
Instrument Fluidic Management
The instrument incorporates the following items to ensure controlled fluid management:
- Dual pipettor arm with air based pipetting—utilizes both capacitive and pressure based fluid detection (LLD) and pressure based dispense verification (RDV).
- A precision dry syringe pump is used to accurately aspirate and dispense volumes from 25 to 1000 µL.
- Built into the pump between the syringe and the pipette tip is a pressure transducer that records the pressure waveform when dispensing and/or aspiration occurs. Characteristics of the curve are used to verify dispense/aspiration process (RDV).
- The conductive pipette tip is attached to the syringe pump through a stainless steel interface that conducts an oscillating current, used to measure changes in capacitance. When the pipette tip touches fluid, the capacitance changes and can be detected through the liquid level detection (LLD) circuitry.
- The fluid levels in the reagent bottles are detected with LLD, and the volume is calculated based on the known bottle geometries.
- The instrument uses precision Auto Detect pumps to ensure accurate Luminometer light off characteristics.
- The Auto Detect pumps has a home sensors to ensure accurate dispensing. Addition of detect reagents is verified through bubble sensors and a light off algorithm.
- The instrument includes Magnetic Wash, oil, and DQ pumps to dispense their respective fluids.
- Verification of wash buffer addition and aspiration (residual volumes) is conducted by means of LLD by the Magnetic Wash aspirator probes. Oil is verified with an in-line pressure sensor.
- All system fluid bottles are located in a drawer under the instrument deck.
- RFID is used to manage the inventory of the universal system fluid bottles.
- Connections to bottles use quick release fittings and are color coordinated.
- Waste fluid is aspirated using a Vacuum Pump.
- A 0.2 micron PTFE sterile air filter ensures that the air flowing out of the Vacuum Pump and into the room is free of biohazard waste.
- A pressure transducer is used to monitor the vacuum pressure at the manifold to ensure that the system is functioning within its operational limits.
- Pump speed control is used to maintain a constant vacuum pressure at the manifold independent of elevation or system wear.
- The waste bottle has empty and full sensors.
